column2: >Video content marketing
column3: >Video marketing is using videos to promote, market your product or service so as to increase engagement on your digital channels and educate your consumers.
column4: >A powerful marketing campaign includes videos into the mix.
column5: > It’s not only on YouTube, but you can also incorporate video marketing just about everywhere. Social media platforms like Facebook, Twitter, Instagram, and Tiktok are also great places for video marketing content.

column2: >Video marketing has been on the scene for a long time, and it’s shown to be profitable for any purpose.
column3: >That means the correct type of video will
column4: >help bring more engagement
column6: >make a video for your business
column7: > but not sure where to start? Check out our top 8 Video Business Ideas.

column2: >Explainer videos are short types of video content marketing, that come in many forms, from 2D to 3D Animation, to live-action and more. They also come in different genres, incorporating comedy or drama depending on the theme. That means there’s a wide variation of design choices and emotional methods to communicate your message.
column3: >Explainer videos are one of the few that tackle several stages of the buyer’s journey at the same time! And they do so by fulfilling a short list of essential characteristics which include being short, visually attractive, simple, and informative.
column4: >Explainer videos are so effective because they combine audio and visual stimuli to explain a concept in a simple and understandable way. Instead of just using audio or text, they use both, which is proven to increase message retention. Explainer videos are so effective because they are concise, show a problem and solution,
column5: >useful for new and old customers alike, adaptable, and show your brand personality.

column2: >A product video is one that expounds and visually displays a product's concrete benefits. A lot of product videos tend to highlight a product's distinctive features, but one main thing that truly differentiates a great product video is its ability to exhibit how it solves issues.
column3: >The aim of preparing a perfect product video is not far off. If you want your video to resonate, it should be about
column4: >more than
column5: > just the product. It should be about the drawbacks, the solution, the experience, and the larger vision of what you're trying to create.
column6: >Whether you’re selling a product or service, the extensive product video can be your success or otherwise.

column2: >A good product video shows a product's features by way of its benefits, telling a story of how that product will impact customers' lives. Product storytelling involves telling the story of a product,  why the organization created it, some of the unique setbacks they faced in doing so, and the impact it has made to their customer's lives.
column3: >Your product story is so much more than an abstract of your product's features. Features don't explain why your product matters (or to whom, or for what reason). Putting out product stories and content around your product has one single purpose- convince and convert.
column4: >You can tell your product story through a story about how it's of use, tried and tested, what it does, Customer product reviews, product’s origin story, stories behind your product's design
column5: >( How a product solves a problem, How it creates usability, Aesthetic and Identity)
column6: >, Does your business have a social purpose? The story of your materials, Stories about who makes your products and so on.

column2: >Seasonal promotional Videos display special offers, discounts, or limited edition items tied to a certain event during the year. This can be a specific holiday such as Thanksgiving, or a certain time of year, such as back-to-school season. So how exactly can you make your seasonal video stand out from the competition, build brand awareness, engage existing customers, and gain new customers for your products?
column3: >Firstly, Align your products with the sentiments your customers have around that time of the year, Offer subscription boxes of your products with specific discounts, Create product bundling campaigns that resonate with customers needs and seasons, combine awareness days with seasonal and holiday promotion campaigns or Appreciate your top tier customers. Successful seasonal-event based videos can help you boost brand awareness, gain new loyal customers, and increase sales.

column2: >Bringing a new product in the market can be the start of a wonderful friendship… or a total debacle. It is a crucial moment that needs all the care and scrutiny it can get. Product launch videos are being used by companies to launch or market their products. A good video incorporated in a product launch strategy makes it brilliant. The tone and style of video will be per your customer base such as promo, teaser, explanation, feature-rich, etc. A good video content marketing strategy start is by looking at what other marketers are creatin. Most product videos include 3D Video, Animated Video, Feature Video, and Launch Teaser video.
>Promotional videos
column3: > are some of the most imaginative, comical, emotional, (and yes, artistic!) pieces of visual storytelling out there today.  A promotional video’s purpose is to promote a specific marketing initiative, sale, or event. Promos are often similar in style and tone to a teaser video, where you grab your audience’s attention and draw them in to learn more. Promo videos are great for attracting new visitors by building awareness online for upcoming events and promotions. If your viewers are new to your brand, a promo video can introduce them to your company by stimulating their interest with your current promotion.

column1: 291,"The power of video marketing for your business | Online Marketing","<span style=""display: none
column2: >Video marketing for your business has become an increasingly popular phenomenon.
column4: >are visual creatures, and we can’t help but be drawn to moving pictures. In the last year, it has been a full-on video marketing revolution year for digital marketing since video boost sales and conversions, and it is the high time every business should understand the power of video as a marketing tool.

column2: >Video marketing attains all the work that traditional marketing does, but it boosts the effects. Video is an adaptable and appealing content format that not only gives us a real-life picture of what is going on
column3: it also helps increase engagement and it is easy to share across different platforms.

column2: >You may ask, Is it really worth considering using videos for promoting your business? The answer is simple: Yes, and here are the reasons why you should be using video marketing as a tool and how it will benefit your business.

>Video continues to take up a larger share of social media content, and why should you care? Because video is one of the most shared contents on social media.  This in turn helps with increasing your social engagement and reaching a bigger audience. Generally, users on platforms like Facebook and Twitter tend to share content that informs and entertains and video is capable of bringing out those two aspects, and that’s why you will find that Facebook places more emphasis on displaying videos on their timelines since that is what most of the audience wants. So are you looking for content that can be shared easily? Try creating videos so as to encourage more shares that will reach a greater audience.

>Video marketing can lead to significant financial payoff. By adding an explainer video on your social media platforms, you can increase engagement (as much as 80% according to some studies). With a great marketing team or Digital Marketing Agency that comprises creatives producing effective videos no longer requires a substantial line in your marketing budget.

>When consumers see you, your team, or your product in videos, they gain more confidence in your brand. Trust is important for every business, and video marketing can be there when you can’t. For any organization, trust from the consumer is crucial and is the foundation of the business. We are at a time when your customers demand more focus on
column3: >kindling, not just content, on trust, not just traffic, and on the loyal people that are advocating for your product out there. Video does it all, it builds trust and brings out emotions since it helps in
column4: >building a relationship through that face to face interaction.

column2: >So, if you feel content marketing is crucial, you must be serious about video, too. Video is a great way to convey your information with your consumers. In just a short time, you can grab their attention, explain what your business does and why they should care. Can you do that in with a whole document of textual content? Yeah, maybe, but you can do it faster and more memorably in a quick video.

column1: 5. Google has a greater affinity towards Videos

column2: >You are 53 times more likely to pop up first on Google if you have a video embedded on your website.  When you have videos on your website, you encourage more people to stay for a longer period of time while they are viewing the videos. This in turn triggers Google search engines to know that you have great content hence improving your SEO.

column1: 6. Video Engages Even the Laziest Buyers

column2: >Video is an excellent way of learning, but it’s also super easy to consume. People are getting too busy to get time to read long product descriptions or go through services. The modern consumer wants to see the product in action. Video preference is one of the most important driving forces of using video in your content marketing hence making it easier for your customers.

column2: >Now, boosting sales on goods and services through video marketing may be an excellent tool, but knowing how to maximize it is a completely different thing.

>You could have the best ideas of what you want it to look like but the end product may be a disaster. Therefore, taking the correct advantage of video marketing as a tool is an art on its own. There are various ways you could employ to ensure you use this tool correctly and ensure its effectiveness:
>First, it is crucial  to know a few basic best practices for your videos:
>Use subtitles in your videos as most people view them with the sound off (on social media)
>Upload your videos natively – on some platforms, you get to reach more people when you upload them natively versus via a tool (plus, make sure to optimize your videos for that specific platform)
>Add your branding: use your logo to watermark your videos and even better.

column1: So what are the ways to Leverage Your Social Media Using Videos?
1. CREATE SHORT VIDEOS TO INFORM YOUR CUSTOMERS

column2: >Putting your information in a short and fun video provides your viewers enough of what they need to know—and if that’s not enough, give them a ‘Learn More’ destination to visit. Whether your video is a tutorial or an overview of a company’s mission, the best content is short and easy to digest.
column3: >Ideally, you can consolidate what you need to say in less than a minute and include a good hook.
column4: >Most importantly, remember that you have less than ten seconds to grab the attention of your audience.

column2: >Facebook and Twitter even made some updates such as better resolutions, player sizes to some of their social sites to push video content into more feeds, and there’s a reason for that.
column3: >Some social sites, such as YouTube and Facebook, encourage organizations to have a featured video or trailer on their web and social platforms.
column4: >Ensure you are uploading your videos natively to every platform you’re active on. The organic reach for video posts is usually higher than simple text and image updates. Also, over time, you can create a broad multimedia library on all platforms, boosting and enhancing brand experience away from your website.

column2: >You’re utilizing video content to show the world what a great business or brand you are, so why not share customer testimonials? Ask your customers to appear in a video and tell their story and experience working with your company. Putting a human face to your brand builds a deeper connection with new and existing audiences.
column3: >Your content will be relatable to a much larger audience and will show off the best parts of your business to the people you want to reach. Make every effort to validate the authenticity of your testimonials, unless you want to appear as if you’ve fabricated these stories.
column4: >Viewers are more intuitive than you think, and spotting a bad actor has become second nature to anyone who has ever been awake at 3 a.m., mesmerized by an infomercial.

column2: >Having a great digital marketing strategy is key for every business in Kenya to ensure growth. Creating an Impact on Social Media is not always easy to achieve.  Companies should focus more on being social than just being on social platforms.
>With the constant emerging tools and platforms, companies can easily fall into the trap of just being tactical with their online marketing instead of being strategic. According to the
column3: > Global Digital Stats and Report
column4: >, there were 22.86 Million internet users in Kenya in January 2020. Social Media Users were 8.80 Million.

column2: >The statistics also showed social media penetration stood at 17% in January 2020. From that information, you can see there is a large audience to tap into. Hence you will need a proper strategy to ensure an effective marketing strategy or plan.
>Here is how you can create a winning social media marketing strategy in 7 Steps. Effective Tips For every business in Kenya.

>Before creating any marketing plan, It’s crucial to first define your objectives before you got into too many details of activities and content. This will help keep you focussed, and also help track how well your marketing strategy is performing.

column5: >Allocating different goals for each social media platform can be highly effective. The reason for this is, user behavior varies in each given platform. A good example, a bakery business might find that activities on Twitter may help you reach customer support goals, whereas on Instagram maybe it’s the best opportunity for social sales.

column2: >Every business is competing for attention on social media. Doing a
column4: >on your competitors on social media platforms can boost your chances of being heard over the noise. You can also learn from what they are doing and spot opportunities.

column2: >Before deciding on your target platform or consumer, it’s crucial to identify where your target audience is currently active. Certain platforms are highly dominated by certain demographics. For example, Pinterest, 81% of users are female, while Twitter, 65.5% of users are male.

column2: >For every marketer, they should always ask themselves, “How did this content help me achieve my goals?”  If you are not analyzing each post to see how it performed then you might not easily tell the impact you are making on social media. column1: 5. Set Up a Social Media Content Calendar

column2: >Before setting up your calendar it is good to first re-evaluate your goals. Once you identify your major goal, maybe it’s brand awareness, dedicate 50% to that given goal. There are certain frameworks to help know how to align your calendar.

>The 80/20 rule states that only 20% of your posts should talk about your brand. The rule of thirds says you should divide social media posts equally between promotional content, thought leadership, and personal interactions. Don't just create promotional content, that can be a turn off to many, creat time for social interactions too and personal attention.
Distribution

column1: What is the Process of Web Design?

column3: > Where the developer works with the client to determine what goals the new website needs to fulfill. I.e., what its purpose is.

column2: >Scope definition:
column3: >I.e., what web pages and features the site requires to fulfill the goal, and the timeline for building those out.

column2: >Sitemap and wireframe creation:
column3: > With the scope well-defined, you can start digging into the sitemap, defining how the content and features we defined in the scope definition will interrelate.

column2: >Content creation:
column3: > Now that you have a bigger picture of the site in mind, you can start creating content for the individual pages, always keeping search engine optimization (SEO) in mind to help keep pages focused on a single topic. It's vital that you have real content to work with for our next stage:

column3: >With the site architecture and some content in place, you can start working on the visual brand. column2: >Testing:
column3: >By now, you've got all your pages and defined how they display to the site visitor, so it's time to make sure it all works. Combine manual browsing of the site on a variety of devices with automated site crawlers to identify everything from user experience issues to simple broken links.

column2: >Launch:
column3: > Once everything's working beautifully, it's time to plan and execute your site launch! This should include planning both launch timing and communication strategies — i.e., when will you launch and how will you let the world know? After that, it's time to break out the bubbly.

column1: Top High performing content used in Digital Marketing in Kenya

Content marketing has become one of the most powerful digital marketing strategies for businesses of all sizes and industries in Kenya. However, when it comes down to developing your marketing strategy, it can be difficult to decide what kind of content marketing you want to use to grow your business. Here are the most common types of content.
Best Digital Marketing Tools for businesses in Kenya.
Marketing tools vary in form and cater to specific functions to help you carry out your marketing strategy.

With so many tools out there, marketing teams can easily get overwhelmed by choosing what they should have in their arsenal. Before jumping off the deep end and giving everything a try at once, consider the following: Who’s your audience? Where’s your audience most likely to be found? What materials will your audience find most useful/engaging? How can you deliver your materials to them in the most efficient way?

There are various marketing tools out there that can take some of the workloads off of your shoulders. These tools are especially valuable for small businesses that don’t have the resources to dedicate a team to in-house marketing, or the budget to outsource the work to a marketing agency.

• Email marketing automation platform- Email marketing platforms, such as MailChimp and Mailerlite, give marketing teams a one-stop-shop for their email marketing needs. With these email marketing tools, users can not only build custom email campaigns, but they can also use list segmentation to build smarter email lists, make use of our analytics and insight feature to monitor the success of campaigns, and test it all before sending.
• Social scheduler platform-These tools are designed to help marketers plan, schedule, and send content out through various social media channels. One platform well known for this is Hootsuite.

• Image design platform-Content is highly crucial in digital marketing and having top-quality imagery to accompany your content is what’ll get you noticed. Canva is one of the image design platforms that offer marketing teams many different options for creating branded materials. Apart from stunning images, you can create various branded materials from posters to fliers.

• Communication and organization platform- Finally, another vital aspect to consider is having a platform that allows you to easily organize your business projects, while also being able to communicate with your workmates. These platforms help you  have a team calendar, a team chatroom, and a Project organizer

column1: How B2B and B2C companies can use Digital Marketing strategies in Kenya

column2: >Digital Marketing is applied by different companies in Kenya in different ways, each to a different degree of success.
column3: >Therefore, different companies — B2B and B2C (Business to Business and Business to Customer) — use Digital Marketing in very varying ways.
column4: >So, what are some of the differences
column5: > between B2B and B2C Digital Marketing strategies?
column6: >Social media has helped bridge the gap between B2B and B2C strategies since companies can now advertise to both companies and customers alike with the same platform and the same strategies.
column7: >The difference between these strategies comes in how they have used and the type of content.The audience
column8: >Customers in the B2B businesses include business owners and managers. In other words, people know a lot about the industry that you are operating in.
column9: >Companies will have to make sure their content does not talk down to these professionals and instead talks to them.
column10: >On the other hand, B2C companies deal with customers who know a lot about the market but do not know the intricacies of the said market.
column11: >Another big difference between B2B and B2C customers is that one is looking for a product or service that has plenty of utility, while the other is looking for the best value.
column12: >B2C customers are often looking for products that give them the most utility for a lower price. However, B2B customers are rarely concerned with the price of a product and look more to its functionality, versatility, and utility.
column13: >B2C companies will mostly choose a very friendly, inviting, and often very casual tone to attract their target audience.
column14: >This tone is also a reflection of the brand’s personality, which is why it is essential to every B2C business.
column15: >These companies will also use platforms like Instagram, Facebook, Pinterest, and even Snapchat — casual and relatable social media suites — to promote their brand.
column16: >B2B companies tend to have a more serious tone and a very straightforward message. These companies use very specific social media platforms like LinkedIn, which is a business platform.Size of the market
column17: >B2C companies are effectively advertising to a massive market with millions of possible customers.
column18: >On the other hand, you have B2B businesses that are always catering to a very specific niche of owners and managers.Relationship with customers
column19: >B2C companies are more concerned with creating brand loyalty and increasing revenue.
column20: >B2B companies have a much more specific criterion that takes higher priority over increasing revenue.

It is not enough to go off hype, take the time to sample your prospective printing companies works and make a judgment from that.
In today's business landscape customer service is everything. Customer service will have a large impact on the experience you have with various prospective printing companies in Kenya.

When choosing a printing company in Kenya consider the way they communicate their product and service offerings to you. They should help you understand your printing needs and how they can deliver them.
They should also make a follow-up if you need some time to consider your options and clearly communicate their timelines and deliverability.
As mentioned in the previous section technology has allowed printing companies in Kenya to evolve and allow printing to be more interactive.

This is something you should consider when choosing a printing company. How much they have evolved and as such how much their service range has evolved. Are they able to print to satisfy all your print business needs?
Be sure to do some research about the prospective printing company's reputation.
An easy way to do this is to simply look at the reviews left by previous customers. Any review above 4.5 stars is a good review and you should consider them for any future business printing projects.
Another great advantage that comes with working with a print company with a great reputation other than getting quality work done,  is that they may have worked with another company in your industry.

This will inform what you need to print. It might also give you ideas that you hadn't thought of or considered and give you ways to improve on what was already done to get your company ahead of the competition.

For most people pricing comes first however when it comes to branding, it should come last on this list. Branding messages are deeply engrained in a customer's mind and so the most important thing is to get it right the first time.
How much it costs you is also something to consider however it's not as high up on the priority list. As long as the price is within the industry standard you have nothing to worry about.

You might be wondering how to figure out the industry standard for business printing projects. The simple way to find out is to get a quote from all the prospective printing companies that check all the other four things on this list of factors to consider.

column1: Step by step live streaming guide for an event in Kenya

column2: >Before engaging  live streaming companies in Kenya, here are the 9 main things you need to understand and do to ensure your live stream event is a success:

>What are you trying to accomplish? Is it to share your story? Increase your sales? Increase awareness for your brand, product, or service? Position yourself as an authority in your niche? Build your following? You have to clearly define why you want to do a live stream before hitting the live broadcast button.

column1: • Define your target audience and message

column2: >Who are you trying to reach and what will your message to them be? Your target audience will determine what platforms, days, times, and communication methods you will use. For example, you will hardly find an individual in their 50s on TikTok at midnight on a Friday. Additionally, an overly playful communication tone will not appeal to them.

>A well-defined audience and message will allow you to plan your platforms and communication in ways that they will resonate with. Do not wait until you are live streaming to decide what your message to your Target Audience will be.

>We highlighted 8 platforms earlier, however, each platform is ideal for specific audiences and goals. If your following is the highest on one platform in comparison to the others, by all means, use that platform. However, sometimes you may want to use a combination of platforms for optimum reach. This decision should be guided by where your followers “hang out” the most frequently and what your goals are. For example, TikTok serves short videos thus if you want to do a live-streamed interview it would not be the ideal platform.

>What will you use? Will it be your PC’s webcam? Will it be an external webcam? Will you use your mobile phone’s camera? What about sound and lighting? Will you need to purchase extra lighting? Will the internal microphone of your PC suffice or will you need to purchase an external one? It is wise to determine the equipment that you will require beforehand. You do not want to find out your lighting is inadequate during the live stream.

>Yes, you need to rehearse! You do not want to face unforeseen technical issues during the live stream. Rehearsing prior will change the status of your technical issues from unforeseen to anticipated. If you know what to expect, you can work around the anticipated issues or find an ideal solution at a good time.

>If your live stream will have guests, prep them on everything that they need to know beforehand. This will mitigate awkward and silent moments during the live stream ensuring that everything flows seamlessly.

column1: • Check your Audio, internet connection, and power

column2: >The worst thing that can happen is to have bad audio and bad internet during a Livestream. Additionally, insufficiently charged devices can throw a spanner in the works. It is best to ensure that you have enough internet bandwidth, power, and great audio.

>Have a monitoring assistant during the Livestream noting and curating your audiences’ sentiments, questions, comments, and requests that will require your addressing during the live event. This is important as you will not have the time to run the event and also pay attention to every comment being shared by your audience. However, you will need to brief your monitoring assistant in advance on what to look out for and bring to your attention.

>To stay connected with your audience, it is best to follow up and thank them for their time. In addition to that, it will also be a great opportunity to alert them about your next live-stream event and where they need to access the needed materials.
>If you adhere to the above 9 steps you will be well on your way to live streaming in Kenya success.

column2: >A webinar is a live-streamed web seminar that encompasses running a conference or presentation online. Just like a physical in-person seminar, most webinars are real-time allowing interaction between the participants.
column4: > is a prerequisite to a successful webinar unless you plan to do an evergreen webinar which we will get to later. A webinar in Kenya presents great opportunities for your business whether B2B or B2C.

column2: >Now that you know what Webinars are, why do you need them?
column3: >Here are some 6 key reasons you should do a webinar:

column2: >It helps you build your prospects and leads database -

>Physical events are one way that organizations build their leads list from and Live events are no different. You might have a following on Facebook, LinkedIn, Twitter, or YouTube but, have they officially given you their contact information for you to directly promote your message, products, or services to them? Everyone who registers for your webinar in Kenya officially gives you their contact information which you can add to your database of warm prospects/leads for your offering.
>Positions you as an expert in your niche

>Webinars allow you to share your expertise with your Target Audience and personally give solutions to their problems. Additionally, interacting with them in person creates trust and you can clear their doubts in regards to any of your offerings. Ultimately, you will come off as a credible source of information in your niche.
>It is easier for you to convert your audience -
>When your audience registers for your webinar, they are expressing interest in your offering. It is thus easier to nurture and eventually convert them seeing that they are already qualified leads.
>Branding opportunities-
>Webinars have countless branding opportunities that will enable your brand to stay top of mind in your audience's minds.
>Promotions

>After you have positioned yourself as an expert in your niche and your audiences trust you and accord you a “tribe” / “cult” like following, you can present your newest products or services to them and they will take them up readily.
>Advocacy

>Sometimes your loyal customer base may have questions regarding your offering and a webinar in Kenya is a great platform to address them because these are the customers who become your brand evangelists.
>Secondly, is to involve them in the solution creation process. Your customers are highly likely to give you insights on how you can improve your current offering to meet their nuanced needs.

column1: How to attract an audience for your webinar?

column2: >One of the key success metrics of a webinar in Kenya is how many attendees one can attract to attend. Here are 7 Pro - tips for how to attract an audience for your webinar:

column1: • Pick topics relevant to your target audience
column2: > -

>At the end of the day, people have pain points that they need to be addressed and if your topic is not specific enough and accurate enough in calling out these pain points and promising a solution then people are unlikely to invest their time.

>What does your audience care about or value? You can hook them with that. It can be offering them a special and valuable freebie once they register. Perhaps a book, case study, report, ticket, or any resource that would have cost them some extra resources to acquire but is free for all webinar attendees.

column1: • Pick the right date and time -

column2: >Attendance numbers can be negatively affected if the date and time for the webinar unfavorable for your audience. Having studied your audience, you are highly likely to know what date and time work for them. Alternatively, you can send out a survey to find out.

>People are highly distracted and you need to ensure that you communicate what your webinar will be about for immediate commitment. A tip to concisely communicate your content and offer is to ask the 5 “W”s: Who? What? When? Where? Why?. This will be a good way to get your webinar in Kenya in the right direction.

>This is extremely key in attracting attendees to your webinar. You can do this in various ways including but not limited to social media marketing, email marketing, and a myriad of other channels. If your target audience does not know it is happening, then it is as good as it never happened.

column1: • Upon attendee registration, send a thank you message, and registration confirmation
column2: > – This may sound obvious, yet it is imperative. It will affirm to your attendees that you acknowledge them and their seat is reserved. Subconsciously they will commit to attending. You can even go further and add a call to action to the message asking them to put the event on their calendar as a commitment device.

column1: • Send reminders as the webinar date approaches -

column2: >Things come up and people forget. Reminders are a good way of keeping your webinar top of mind in your Audience’s mind irrespective of their daily distractions. You can go ahead and also remind them of the value that they will be getting to keep them eager.

column1: 12 best practices of running successful webinars in Kenya

column2: >The 12 main things that will ensure your webinar live events are a success are :
>Knowing your target audience  -

>Who are you trying to appeal to? This is very important. Your target audience will determine what platforms, what content, which speakers, and what dates and times will be relevant to them in regards to your webinar. Knowing your Target audience can
column3: >save you a lot of time, money and effort
column4: >.  There many ways to do this and you can have a professional
column6: > to help you clearly define your target audience.

column2: >Picking a relevant topic -

>If your webinar topic does not inform and engage your audience then you will be wasting your time and their time. Your audience wants to know if your webinar will be relevant to their needs and pain points. You should communicate this through your chosen topic. You can do this by using some of the most common questions they pose around your offering via social media, calls to your customer support lines, email queries, and other relevant channels.
>Deciding on your webinar format
>Will you be presenting yourself? Will you be presenting as a panel? Will you be presenting as dual presenters? Will it be a Q&
column3: A webinar? Will it be a product demonstration or launch? Will it be an interview where you will invite experts who are popular and credible to enlighten your audience on specific matters? The format is entirely dependent on what you plan to accomplish and it should offer the most value to your attendees.

column2: >Finding relevant speakers - Depending on the format, you may be inviting guests to the Webinar and it will be crucial to find speakers who will be relevant to your target audience. The key is ensuring that the speaker has knowledge and experience in what they will be sharing with your audience. Additionally, they should be well known for their expertise in their niche to ride on their credibility and pull more numbers to the webinar.

>Setting an appropriate date and time- Depending on your geographical location and the culture that pertains therein, setting an appropriate date and time for your webinar is key because this will make it easier for your attendees to commit due to their availability.
>Getting expert help -

>An expert who understands webinar software and equipment is invaluable as a partner. This is because you are likely to go crazy trying to do everything yourself. You can focus on the content, guests, and attendees and they can focus on the technicalities of the live event. This will ensure everything unfolds seamlessly from planning to execution and monitoring.

>Doing the dry run- Things will go wrong. This is a given. To ensure that your guests, your technical team, and yourself are aligned and on top of the game, rehearsing is important. Furthermore, you need to ensure that all your tools and equipment are working properly. You do not want to find out that your slides are not in order and your sound is terrible on the day of the webinar.
>Marketing and promoting your webinar
>Okay, you have a great event coming up but, who cares if they do not know?

>You have to think about your marketing and promotion. On one hand, you do not want to waste time and money communicating your webinar to the wrong audience, and on the other hand, you do not want to miss communicating about it to the right audience. You should have a professional marketing and communications team planning and executing your marketing and promotion. It will save you a lot of time and money.
>Planning time for interaction during the webinar

>Your webinar will happen so fast that if you do not allocate time purposefully for interaction with the audience this opportunity will be missed. After listening to a speaker for 30 minutes or more your audience may get distracted or bored. Encouraging them to participate through scheduled challenges, poll questions, discussions and other tactics will ensure their attention till the end of the webinar.
>Offering a Call to action after the webinar

>What is the next step that you want your audience to take? You have to communicate this. A call to action can include but is not limited to joining the next webinar, starting a free trial for your offering, making a purchase of your product or service, requesting a quote/consultation, and so forth.
>Tracking and monitoring results

>How many people attended your webinar against those who registered? Where did they hear about the webinar from? Did some drop off during the webinar or did all stay on till the end? How many answered the call to action? These and many other metrics are important in understanding how best to optimize your future webinar experience for your audience. Ensure that you know what metrics will be important for you to track beforehand.

>Asking for feedback- Do you want to improve moving forward? Ask for feedback! A simple survey after the webinar will do the job. Knowing if your attendees loved or hated your event and what they think could be improved will allow you to make informed future decisions.

>An evergreen webinar is also known as an automated webinar. It is a recorded and automated webinar instead of it being live. The content of evergreen webinars should ideally focus on principles or foundational practices of a niche that will never be affected by the changing trends or fads. Here are some advantages to setting up an evergreen webinar series:
>Nurturing new subscribers

>While the session will not be live, an evergreen webinar will allow your subscribers to get to the person behind the business(which is you) more even in your real-time absence. They will grow to trust you more as they keep learning and getting value from you through the webinar.
>Passive income

>If you include a registration fee to get access to your webinar and also promote your other products or services within your webinar, you will be making money in your sleep, or while on vacation. Evergreen Webinars are a great way of making passive income because they are AUTOMATED which leads us to the next benefit…
>Low maintenance-

>The initial work in setting up an evergreen webinar will be equivalent, if not more, to a live webinar however, once that is done it runs on autopilot! You will be required to check in occasionally to ensure everything is running as expected.
>Great for positioning yourself as an authority in your niche -

>If you have a lot of value to offer your audience around your niche why not do it 24/7 and 365 days a year? With evergreen content, your automated webinars will be interacting with your audience and building your credibility in your absence.
>Now that you have an exhaustive understanding of running a successful webinar in Kenya you probably want to get started right away.

Before we look at the Top Research Companies in Kenya, you must understand what is entailed when doing Market Research in Kenya. There are various steps your organization should understand before undertaking research in Kenya and the African market at large.

column2: >Market research is an undertaking that involves the gathering of data, its analysis, and interpretation through a set of techniques to allow a business to either discover its target market or to understand it better. A business can do marketing research on its own, or, it can employ the expertise of a third-party company that specializes in marketing research.

column1: Why do Market research for your organization in Africa?

column2: >Businesses employ marketing research to get information that will allow them to create better products/services, improve customer/ user experience, and optimize marketing communication to better achieve the communication goals whether it is attracting quality leads or getting better conversions.
column3: >Ultimately, marketing research helps businesses to understand how to best position their products and services favorably towards their target market, and here are 5 crucial reasons you should be doing marketing research:

column2: >In-depth customer understanding

>Do you know who will buy your product or service and where you can find them? Do you know their expectations? Do you know the price points they will be comfortable with and how often they will be willing to purchase from you? Do you have a clear picture of your ideal customer persona?  Do you know how many of your ideal customers exist in the market you plan to distribute your products in? Marketing research will help you answer all these questions and you will be well on your way to creating effective sales and marketing campaigns.
>Competitor analysis -

>Do you know who your competitors are? Do you know the price points for their products and services? Do you know their market positioning? Do you know their approach to the market? Marketing research will help you answer all these questions and allow you to either find gaps in your competitor’s strategies that you can capitalize on or learn from their working strategies and perfect them to work even better for you.
>Market feasibility study -

>You do not want to launch a product or service then discover that the market is not ready for it or will not take it up for one reason or another. Market research helps you test your idea or product before you launch it into the market.
>If market research is done correctly, your product or service will instantly connect with your target audience because you would have perfected both the offering and go to market strategy.
>Business growth

>Customer demands change and products go through a product life cycle that spans from introduction to decline. These things are inevitable and continuous market research allows you to either improve existing products/services to keep up with customer demands or introduce new products/services to replace the ones at the decline stage.
>This will keep your business growing and you will scale into new markets and new industries irrespective of where you initially began.
>The Marketing research process has six steps as outlined in the table below:
>1.Defining the problem or opportunity

>The outcome here is clarifying what you are trying to learn from the research. Maybe you want to know how many potential buyers exist in a certain locality because there seems to be an opportunity there but the problem is you do not have statistical data that will allow you to confidently decide to enter that market. Maybe you need to understand what age groups, gender, occupations are the top promoters of your offering to target them better and you do not have this information. The problem/opportunity could be anything and you need to clearly define it.
>2. Developing the Research Plan

>The outcome here is to determine both the sources of data and methods of data collection that will be relevant to your research objectives which were clarified in step one. Will secondary data suffice or will you need primary data and what will be your sampling plan and methods of contacting and engaging respondents? This needs to be clear as day before moving on to step 3.
>3.Collecting data

>The outcome here is having data and information that is relevant to your research objectives. It can be either qualitative or quantitative or both. This is the most crucial step of the process and requires the most investment in terms of time and money.
>4. Analysing the Data
>The outcome here is organized data that can be analysed through human interrogation or advanced data analysis tools. This is dependent on the extent and complexity of the data collected.
>5.Presenting the findings

>The outcome here is reporting the results of the research in summarized formats that can facilitate decision making from key decision-makers possibly in research and development, marketing and management.
>6. Making informed decisions

>The outcome is putting the analysis into action. Did you find that women aged 32-40 years from the coastal region appear to be the leading force among your customers? Then expand into that region and tailor-make products or marketing messages to them! The possibilities could be endless, however, after research, the findings need to be able to influence decisions and recommendations need to be actionable.

column1: 469,"7 Steps Checklist To Measure The Performance Of Your Digital Marketing","

column2: >Peter Drucker, a management thinker is often quoted saying,” you cannot manage what you cannot measure.” However, for the sake of this checklist to measure the performance of your digital marketing, we will go further and echo the words of Lord Kelvin, a physicist and mathematician of the 20
column4: > century, “What is not defined cannot be measured. What is not measured, cannot be improved. What is not improved, is always degraded.”

column2: >In digital marketing, you need to define what success looks like following your digital marketing efforts and find ways of tracking this to successfully measure the performance of your activities and eventually improve them. Otherwise, your efforts will be useless.
>Here is a 7 step checklist to measure the performance of your digital marketing campaigns that will ensure your brand management efforts pay off.

column1: Step 1 – Start by determining your business objectives

column2: >What are your business goals? Pro-Tip: Every single person in your organization must be aligned with regard to your business objectives.
>Furthermore, ensure that your business objectives are Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant and Time-bound (
column4: >).

column2: >Each business will have goals unique to their needs. However, the top 5 business objectives that may advise your marketing efforts are:
>Revenue Growth -
>This is the % increase in your sales revenues from one period to the next that you are aiming for. An example of SMART objective is: To generate 28% revenue increase from online sales between 1
column4: > and 31 December compared to a similar period last year.

column2: >Customer Satisfaction
>This is the extent to which your product or service meets or exceeds your customer’s satisfaction.
>Return on Investment -
>This is the ratio between the net profit you make and the cost incurred to make that profit. It can be used to measure the effectiveness of an investment.
>Customer Retention -

>Customer retention rate metrics are a measure of the number of customers that your business continues to do business with over a given period. It is closely related to repurchase rates and that too can be a business objective.
>Customer Acquisition

>Customer acquisition is the recruitment of new customers into purchasing your products or services. It involves bringing consumers down the marketing funnel from brand awareness to purchase decisions.

column1: Step 2 – Map your business objectives to Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)
column2: >This is identifying key metrics that you can easily use to track and measure your identified business objectives.
column3: >As a demonstration, the table below maps out the various digital marketing KPI metrics that can be used to track the business objectives identified in step 1.

column2: >Revenue Growth
>Online sales per day, online sales per region, online sales per channel, and, online sales per period.
>Customer Satisfaction
>Customer satisfaction score, Net Promoter Score, and Sales team response time.
>Return on Investment
>ROI Value and ROI Rate
>Customer Retention
>Repeat purchase volume and Repurchase Rate
>Customer Acquisition
>Conversion Rate, click through rates, Cost of Customer Acquisition, leads to SQLs ratio, SQL to closed customer ratio, and Check out abandonment rate.

>KPI setting for your business objectives should take into consideration all the activities, products, or services showcased via your digital presence e.g. Website, App, Landing page, Social media, Et cetera. This can range from simply creating brand awareness or positioning or it can be results-oriented like generating leads and increasing conversion rates. Step 3 – Measure
column3: >Having identified the most appropriate metrics that you need to track, you will need to identify tools that capture these metrics and start tracking them. Most digital and social media platforms already have their inbuilt tools for analytics and you may just need to employ them. In other cases, you will need to employ the use of 3
column4: >rd
column5: > party tools and in extremely rare cases, build your own using APIs. Step 4 – Optimize
column6: >The digital space allows for real-time optimization of marketing efforts. As you track and measure what is working, optimize your efforts for maximum gain. Simply tone down what is not working and amplify what is working.
column7: >Simply ask: How are my metrics doing? Am I missing anything? Was anything redundant or unnecessary? Figure out what you can do better, make modifications, and then keep measuring to track results. Keep asking yourself: Are my metrics helping me address my business objectives or do I need to rethink them?

column2: >You will need to determine an appropriate method for reporting your progress to your team and business stakeholders. This includes what to report, which reporting tools are appropriate, and the regularity of reporting.

>If you are reporting to business stakeholders with little digital experience, then reporting on a monthly basis using a presentation slide deck whose contents simply map out the overarching digital contribution to the rest of the business works. This could be your board or your senior management officials like CEO, President, or CFO.

>Nonetheless, if you are reporting to stakeholders who are well versed in the digital space and thus their decision-making will be aided by the granular details of your marketing activities then it is best to report metrics down to the platform level. If social media reporting granular details even at the post level is ideal. Such stakeholders could include but not limited to your CMO, SEO specialist, account managers, and business partners. The reporting tools could range from spreadsheets to presentation slides. It will depend on the kind and amount of data being presented.

column1: Step 6 – Use team and business stakeholder feedback to improve and experiment

column2: >Your team and your stakeholders may challenge you or give you insights that simply never occurred to you. Take this feedback and improve your digital marketing efforts. Furthermore, you can experiment to determine what might work better. One great way that you can experiment to improve your digital marketing performance is:
> – This is when you compare the original version of the item (AD Creative) to a newly changed item (Green CTA instead of previous Blue CTA).
>A/B testing helps you see how your change performs in comparison compared to the original. It’s the most ideal way to prove if something you suspect will work better actually works better or not.

>When all the above steps are executed correctly, it is assured that your digital marketing efforts will be contributing to your business’s bottom line. The final step is to ensure that you have noted everything that works for your business in the previous six steps and replicates them moving on. This will create a proven system that you can repeat over and over again to drive results.

column1: 471,"5 Step Checklist To Creating Videos That Brings Customer Conversions.","

column2: >The power of video marketing for your business
column3: > cannot be understated. In this day and age, having a content marketing strategy that does not employ creating videos that convert is simply shooting your content marketing efforts in the foot. People have a greater affinity towards video content and so do search engines. Furthermore, if well-executed, videos have excellent ROI.

column2: >If you have determined that you need to employ the use of videos that convert in your marketing efforts, here is a 5 step checklist to creating videos that convert views to paying customers.

column1: Step 1 – Use content ideas that are already converting

column2: >No need to reinvent the wheel (unless you have to for some reason), because there already exists a myriad of tested and proven content ideas that are already driving conversions for digital marketers. Where can you find these highly converting ideas? Depending on your niche, look for brands with successful:
><span style=""font-weight: 400
><span style=""font-weight: 400
><span style=""font-weight: 400
><span style=""font-weight: 400
><span style=""font-weight: 400
><span style=""font-weight: 400
><span style=""font-weight: 400
><span style=""font-weight: 400
>Once you identify at least 3 top brands in your niche and identify winning content ideas that they all employ, you will get a feel for what content ideas to run with and what to shelve.
column3: >Pro-tip for highly converting video content: The value proposition is strong, it is relevant to the needs and expectations of the viewer, and the call to action is simple and clear. Step 2 – Keep it short with strategically placed CTAs
column4: >On the internet, many distractions try to grab the attention of netizens. While watching your video, ads will run, pop-ups will appear, other suggested videos will be shown and the viewer might get bored or distracted based on their psychological activities. With this in mind, your videos should be short and punchy with a strategic call to action (CTA) that directs your viewer to the next actionable step.
column5: >Your video should not be your entire pitch. You are likely to lose your viewer before they convert. Chunk the process for them in a simple and actionable manner.
column6: >Your Video CTA can lead them to a landing page where you brief them of a time-bound offer just for them or any other offer for that matter. If they take the action of taking advantage of the offer you may then cross-sell or upsell them. If this were an entire video, the path to conversion is going to be long and boring for your viewer. Step 3 – Do thorough Video Search Optimization
column7: >Before posting your video, do some keyword research to determine which keywords would generate the most views. You can use free tools like Google Keyword planner or get paid tools. Once you identify the most ideal keywords, ensure that you incorporate them in your video title and description.
column8: >Furthermore, you can use relevant keywords in the content of the video and then add subtitles or closed caption files to the video for improved search rankings. It will also ensure your viewer accurately understands your message because they will both read and listen to it.

column1: Step 4 – Distribute your video via multiple platforms

column2: >First off, to distribute your video via multiple platforms, you MUST optimize it for the platforms in question. Nowadays, viewers are everywhere. Your website or YouTube is not the exclusive place where they should access your video content. Web, Mobile, and various social networks are all the places your videos should appear.

>The customer’s buyer journey is not a straight path. You need to reach them across multiple touchpoints for them to finally convert. If you use only one or very few touchpoints, you are unlikely to push them through your sales funnel until they make a purchase.

column1: Step 5 – Experiment with different things and see what sticks

column2: >On which platforms should your video appear? Which social networks are best for your video? How long should your video be? What content should your video contain? How should you do your audience targeting? You may be having many questions about what will and will not work for you. Step one pointed you in the right direction because you will get a feel for some standard practices in your niche.

>Nonetheless, know those different audiences have different video consumption nuances and through practice, you will get a knack for what works for your audience. Rome was not built in a day and practice makes perfect.

>Furthermore, the most important thing to do is to experiment. Test out different ideas and see what sticks for your audience. Once you hit the sweet spot scale that practice and keep optimizing. With experimentation, you may learn that your audience responds to long videos for specific types of content and short videos for other kinds of content. Furthermore, you may find that they respond to certain CTAs better than others.
>Pro-Tip: Conducting A/B tests and tracking how they’re performing is the best way to go about experimentation.

column2: >In this day and age, having a business without a digital presence is like opening a business and not telling anyone. 81% of people search online for a product or service. Let us say that you have determined that you need to launch your brand online because you want to make it easier for potential customers to find you, make it easier to showcase your product/ services, or, make it easier to market your brand, where do you begin?

column1: Step 1 – Start by analyzing your target audience

column2: >How well you understand your target market is imperative to the success of your digital activities. This is because your target market is the one who will become your core Target Audience online. Remember, your product or service serves someone’s needs. Ask yourself
column3: Who is this person? Why do they choose my offering? How can I better serve them? Where do they hang out online? Who else do they go to for solutions to their pinpoints other than me?

column2: >Not everybody wants your offering. If you do not have a clear target audience in mind, your digital customer acquisition costs are likely to be higher than necessary. column1: 494,"5 Simple Ways to Get B2B Contacts in Kenya","<span style=""font-weight: 400
column2: >Globally, the business-to-business (B2B) e-commerce sector is 5 times the size of business-to-consumer (B2C).
column3: >Research shows that there is great potential for the African B2B sector to grow tremendously in the coming days.

column2: >For many B2B ventures, particularly SMEs, the path to achieving success in this sector is long, winding and full of challenges.
column3: >One area many businesses struggle with is lead generation. In the past, all you had to do was go over a local business directory to find business contact information.
column4: >Today, however, there are numerous options you can pursue with varying levels of success.

column2: >Let’s examine the ways you can get contacts of B2B prospects in Kenya.

column1: 1. Looking up Prospects’ B2B Contacts On Search Engines

column2: >One way to get B2B contacts in Kenya is through online queries. In an ideal scenario, once you make your request, search engines like Google and Bing would crawl websites on the internet, index the data they pick up and show you the exact contact details of your B2B prospects.
column3: >In reality, however, this isn’t the case. The search engine's ability to display this information is pegged on the contact details being available in the first place. Moreover, some businesses prevent crawling on their websites and pages, limiting how much search engines can display to you.
column4: >Depending on how well laid out a prospect’s online presence is, the contact information you receive may not be accurate or up to date. Alternatively, you can use
column7: >tools that have a search portal where you can help you get contact information of your leads based on job titles or industry.

column1: 2. Searching for B2B Contacts on LinkedIn

column2: >LinkedIn has cemented itself as the go-to social networking platform for professionals and organizations.
column3: >Given its revolutionary impact on networking, B2B marketers have turned to it as a potential source for B2B leads and contacts.
column4: >However, there are certain limitations you’re bound to encounter using LinkedIn in this manner.
column5: >LinkedIn users in professional circles tend to restrict the number of connection requests they accept. Accepting many requests even from sources they aren’t acquainted with builds a large network, but not necessarily one that’s meaningful.
column6: >The other obstacle in using LinkedIn to get B2B contact details is privacy. LinkedIn’s settings enable users to restrict who can view or export their email address as shown below:
column7: >Due to growing data privacy concerns, your prospects may have prevented the public exposure of their contacts. As such, getting this information yourself or through LinkedIn extraction tools isn’t possible.

column2: >Technology has altered the manner in which we can get leads. Lead generation software such as Uplead optimizes the processes of getting B2B contacts.
column3: >So how does lead generation software work? Most tools require you to sign up at a fee in order to access the B2B contacts they have gathered over time.
column4: >The drawback of using this method is that lead generation tools are not tailored to cater to markets such as Kenya. Again, many of these tools rely on the online availability of contact details without which they can’t generate the results you need.

column2: >If you’re looking to get B2B contacts of prospects without incurring the high costs associated with software tools, there are some contact databases available online.
column3: >However, these are far from ideal for two key reasons. One, they mostly infringe on privacy. Majority of these databases get data through unsavoury practices from third party data collected without consent to phishing.
column4: >Two, there’s a high likelihood that messages you send to email addresses gathered in this way can trigger security filters. Your well-crafted B2B emails, therefore, end up in spam folders.

column1: Importance of creating a buyer persona for your online ads

column2: >Now that you have somewhere to start with the buyer persona let’s briefly discuss why it’s important to create a buyer persona.
>It informs the advertising message

>In the process of creating a buyer persona, you might realize that you have very different groups of customers and this is important because it will inform the advertising message you create, the tone and type of language you use as well as the channel you use for your online advertising.
>It tells you where to find your customers
>Creating a buyer persona gives you a hint as to where you can find your target customer for your internet ads.

>For instance, if your persona is between 18 and 34 years then chances are you will probably get them on Instagram, if your buying persona is between 35 and 65 years then you can get them on Facebook and if your persona is mostly working professionals then chances are you will get them on LinkedIn.
>All that aside, all these different age groups have one thing in common, they all use search engines and online websites. That is where Google ads and pay-per-click or PPC advertising come in.

>2. Select channels for your online ads
>Once you have created a customer persona you’ll have a pretty good idea of where to put your online ads. You will advertise on platforms that your buyer persona frequents.
>Some avenues for you to explore are search engines/Google Ads, social media advertising, and Pay-per-click advertising.

column1: Online advertising in Kenya through Google Ads

column2: >There are factors to consider to make sure you get the most returns from your online advertising in Kenya. Let’s begin with search engine ads/Google Ads.

>For Google ads, you’ll have to do something called keyword search. Many tools can help you do this with Google’s Keyword Planner and Moz’s keyword search tools at the top of the list. Here are links to free keyword search tools.
>https://ads.google.com/home/tools/keyword-planner/
>https://moz.com/explorer
>https://keywordtool.io/
>You might be tempted to go for all the high-traffic keywords but don’t. Instead, you should focus on many long-tail keywords that are more specific to your product or service offering.
>Why is this a better strategy?
>Because the customers who are looking for long-tail searches want something more specific and are more likely to be ready to make a purchase.

column2: >What is the 80/20 rule of posting?

>It’s the rule that says that you should post 80% of content that adds value to your audience for example tips and hacks that have to do with using your products or how to care for them and things of that nature. Then 20% can be ad banner-type posts.
>This is how you build your platform organically and build a community around your brand on social media.

>Simply fill in all the required fields and schedule the ads to go live when your target customers are engaging with the app and your marketing success is all but guaranteed.
>Buy-sell ads/Direct buy ads are when you rent out space on someone’s platform to advertise and pay them per click or per a thousand clicks.

column1: 498,"How to use Facebook stories for business in Kenya: The ultimate guide","<span style=""font-weight: 400
column2: >Have you been wondering how you can use Facebook stories for your business in Kenya? If you have, way to think ahead of the competition.

>Facebook stories are an asset that can prove invaluable to your business when utilized to its full potential. In this post, we look at how your business can tap into the goldmine that is Facebook stories.
>Facebook Stories are short user-generated photo, audio, and video collections that disappear after 24 hours.
>Why are Facebook stories important for your business in Kenya?
>Creating stories can seem unnecessary especially if you are already posting frequently and advertising on Facebook which begs the question why? Why are Facebook stories important for your business?
column3: >In this section, we’ll look at 5 reasons why you should be using Facebook stories for your business in Kenya.

column2: >1. Increase your brand reach

>The first reason is that Facebook stories will increase your reach. Customers who don’t engage with your posts on your feed will definitely see you at the top of their page when they are scrolling through stories.
>2. Get closer to your customers
>Unlike posts, stories have a much more relaxed feel. Facebook tories give you the opportunity to connect with your customers on a real-time basis.
>3. Make your business appear more human

>It is becoming increasingly important for businesses to appear more human and authentic. Customers’ priorities have changed in terms of what motivates them to become loyal to a brand. They are spoilt for choice and therefore, bands have to try harder to create loyalty.
column3: >One such method is to present your brand’s human side through Facebook stories.

column2: ab_channel=SocialMediaWorldwide
>4. Answer customer questions in real-time

>Another reason why you should use Facebook stories for your business in Kenya is that it will allow you to answer customer questions in real-time. Posting stories requires you to be on the platform unlike posting regular posts which can be done with a marketing automation tool.
column3: >Sometimes the difference between a customer making a purchase and not making a purchase is a question which a customer has. Being able to answer that question could mean a sale for you.

column2: >5. Promote user-generated content

>Facebook stories are also a great avenue to promote user-generated content. Posting user-generated content to your feed could easily affect your branding or simply the aesthetic you have worked hard to create on your profile.
column3: >However, with Facebook stories, you can share user-generated content which presents social proof without consequence.

column2: >How to create Facebook stories for your business in Kenya
>While you can post Facebook stories from your Laptop you will get the most options while posting from your smartphone o that is what we recommend.
>Step 1. Choose the type of Facebook story content you want to create
>When creating a Facebook story, you’ll have the option to choose from different types of content formats, or you can also choose to upload an existing photo or video from your gallery.
column3: >Facebook offers several different formats and tools for your stories content. Gallery for sharing existing photos or videos on your phone. Boomerang for taking a burst of photos and turning them into an animation. Text for creating a text-based story.
column4: >Layout for posting multiple photos in different grids or collage configurations. Superzoom for zooming in on a subject. Poll for conducting viewer polls between two options.
column5: >The top row options and the blue camera icon in the bottom right corner give you two access points for those different story formats. However, when you click the blue camera icon, you can also take pictures or record videos, boomerangs, or Facebook live videos.

column2: >Step 2. Get creative with your content

>Facebook offers plenty of creative tools to make your stories pop. So you can play around with these options before you finish creating your story. Find these fun add-ons on the right-hand column after you’ve selected an image file or taken a new picture or video.
>Step 3. Add custom links and buttons

>What separates Facebook stories on profiles versus Pages is the ability to share links. So for those using Facebook stories for business, there are several links and buttons that are crucial for marketing.
column3: >By tapping the link icon on the right sidebar, you can choose from a few call-to-action buttons and customize them for viewers to interact with. Encourage people to book now, call, get directions, shop, and much more.

column2: >Step 4. Share your Story
>Once you’re satisfied with your creation, tap on “Share Now.” That’s it you’ve created and shared your Facebook story.
>Best practices for creating Facebook stories for your business in Kenya
>While knowing the basics of how to post Facebook stories is essential, it is not enough to crush the competition. It is important to adhere to the best practices shared below.
>1. Create exciting, time-sensitive content

>The “urgency factor” is what makes stories such a popular feature because of their 24-hour availability. Take advantage of this to create time-sensitive content that can build excitement and urgency.
column3: >Examples of such could include promoting a 24-hour sale with a code, share early bird offers, get people to sign up for an event, and more.

column2: >2. Make it interactive and actionable

>Because stories can draw in a large audience, create opportunities for engagement by using interactive tools like polls and voting stickers. Stories are an opportunity to get closer to your customers and answer any questions they might have.
ab_channel=LYFEMarketing
>3. Share user-generated content

>Stories are the place for you to showcase your happy customers and any reviews you get from them. It is the place to celebrate the people who keep your business doors open and that includes your employees.
column3: >Adding stories to your already heavy posting schedule can seem overwhelming but you can start with one story a week and increase as you get used to posting them. Three stories a week is ideal.
column4: >Unlike feed posts, stories require real-time engagement so keep that in mind when you begin posting Facebook stories for your business.

column1: 528,"Effective Landing Page Design - 5 Step Guide","

column2: >Effective landing page design is one of the most underestimated steps of a digital marketing strategy.
>With Kenya’s internet users reaching
column3: >21.75 million users as of January 2021
column4: >, Kenyan businesses are in a constant battle to get their share of attention from these users.

column2: >Whether your audience is coming from search, social or email, your landing page is where users will either be drawn further to your offer or be put off and end their buying journey abruptly.
>Before we discuss the attributes of an effective landing page , let’s begin by making sure you are clear about what a landing page is.
><span style=""font-weight: 400
>When we talk about a landing page, we are talking about a page that a user lands on, an entrance page.
column3: >This is the first page a user sees after having clicked some kind of ad source. It could be a PPC ad, a banner in an email, or a link from social media.
column4: >Landing pages work independently of the rest of a website or app. They are focused on a clear conversion goal.

column2: ><span style=""font-weight: 400
>Up to 58% of Kenyans are using social or search as sources of brand discovery. These sources are leading them to entrance pages. What is making some pages outperform others?
>An effective landing page does what it is supposed to do, that is to shorten the journey from click to conversion.
>Instead of sending your users to a home page where they would have to scroll several layers of navigation to get to the product you showed them in an ad, we are taking them straight to that offer.
>Effective landing page design follows up on the promise made in an ad source. It speaks to user motivation and it addresses
column4: >.

column2: >By answering important questions for the user, we create clarity and a clear path to the conversion goal.

column1: 5 Steps to Effective Landing Page Design

column2: >Step 1: Determine the goal of your landing page
>As mentioned earlier, your landing page needs to be focused on ONE specific goal.
column3: >Some of the most common landing page goals include the following:

column2: ><span style=""font-weight: 400
column3: >Lead Generation - Choose this if your main focus is to collect information from visitors through a contact form when they fill out requests for your services.

column2: >Brand Awareness - You can use viral landing pages that are easily shareable on social media by your users. This drives tons of organic traffic to your site.
>Growing your Email List - Adding a lead magnet, such as a free download available after visitors complete a form, is a great way to grow your email list for email marketing.

>Information/Education - If you do not sell anything online, but would still like to inform your audience about your business, you can use this type of landing page which will act as a digital business card giving visitors “About Us” information.

column2: >Step 3: Effective Landing Page Design Includes Content That Attracts and Converts
>Now that you have the right design sorted, it is time to add content to it.
><span style=""font-weight: 400
>The first item to work on is your title. You want a strong title for your landing page. One that clearly communicates your offer and is in line with your objectives.
column3: >The best titles make use of one or a combination of these techniques:

column2: >Use your hero screen to state precisely what your business is about.
>Make your audience open up by asking them a question about their pain points which you have a solution for.
>What is your unique selling point? Why should users choose your offer over others?
>Curiosity is a strong driver, telling your visitors that you intend to reveal something to them can motivate them to explore the rest of your content.

column1: • Making use of “Fear of Missing Out”

column2: >Use limited time offers that stress the significance of the value of your offer..

column1: 563,"Top 5 Best HR Management Software in Kenya","

column2: >Looking to enhance human resource operations in your organization? Read on for a comprehensive look at the best HR management software in Kenya.
>What Is Human Resource Management Software?
>The events of 2020 have resulted in a phenomenon dubbed the
column4: >. Our sudden reliance on digital tools has only escalated the already rapid adoption of technology in almost every aspect of modern life.
column5: >HR hasn’t gone untouched. While payroll management systems have been in use for the better part of the past couple of decades, now, you’d be at odds to find an aspect of human resource management that isn't digitized.
column6: >As HR departments continue to deal with growing responsibilities and increased complexity in their work, solutions have arisen in the form of software.
column7: >HR Management Software programs - also dubbed as HRIS - automate HR activities. Therefore, they make the crucial task of managing people more feasible.

column2: >Key Features of a Good HR Management Software
>Before choosing from our roundup of the best HR management software in Kenya, it’s important to go over some attributes you should consider.
>Integration
>Integration, the ability to use one tool with another or a set of others, is an important factor to evaluate.
column3: >HR management software that can integrate with other software or scaled across different devices/environments would be a good choice.
column4: >This is partly attributed to the variance in capabilities of HRIS. You may find great software that would be easy to implement but lacks certain features you need. Still, if it checks the integration check-box, you don’t have to forgo it. You can use it with the other integrated tools to make up for any shortcomings the otherwise stellar HRIS may have.
