column3: >Ideally, you should be able to create unique user-profiles and keep track of a person’s role, duties, pay rises, promotions and pensions as well as other key data.

column2: >Online Learning

>Continuous development of an organization’s workforce should be a primary concern. One way to action this, particularly in present times, is by availing courses and similar learning materials. A comprehensive HR management software will have this as part of its offering, making it possible for employees to acquire new skills, polish up on what they already know and keep discovering new ideas to help them achieve their full potential. As part of this, the feature set might include progress tracking, grading and certification.

column3: >If you’re wondering whether or not to invest in these tools, let’s examine the potential benefits you stand to accrue.Time-Saving:

column6: > Certain employee attributes can be managed directly by them and the benefit is two-fold. On one hand, employees get more control over their information while enjoying convenience. On the other, the HR department decreases part of the workload. It’s a definite win-win for everyone.Competitive Edge:
column7: > To stay ahead of the competition, you need to not only attract but also retain the top talent in your industry. With good HR management software, you can better manage your organization’s human resources, thereby gaining an edge. Employee Development:
column8: > As mentioned above, HRIS provides an opportunity to grow and develop employees. As part of your employee development efforts, you can offer rewards, set up team-building challenges and provide useful resources to motivate and inspire your organization’s workforce.

column2: >Online advertising in Kenya also allows you to customize and optimize your advertising message.

column5: >Organic marketing uses SEO, social media, and a variety of other channels to increase brand awareness.

>Over black Friday month did you happen to get a message from JUMIA? Or Kilimall? Or perhaps Uber eats?

>Retargeting and Remarketing
>The seventh most common type of online advertising in Kenya is retargeting and remarketing.
column3: >Although retargeting and remarketing are similar, they are not the same thing.

column2: >Retargeting
>Retargeting refers to online ad placement or display ads targeting users who have interacted with your site in specific ways without purchasing.
column3: >Once a visitor enters your website, clicks on a product, or takes a certain action that you want them to take, a cookie is set in their browser. You
column4: > can then use this information to “retarget” them with ads based on their interactions once they leave your site.
column5: >These ads are placed by third parties, such as the Google Display Network or Facebook. They allow your ads to trigger on other sites that your visitors go to.

column2: >Remarketing
>Remarketing is when you send a targeted ad to a customer who has already purchased your product or service.
column3: >Remarketing ads are typically used to get the customer to purchase again or to upsell them to a higher product offering. The messaging uses their previous purchase to inform and customize the message.
column4: >The key thing to note about the difference between retargeting and remarketing is that retargeting is to people who have not yet purchased your products while remarketing is to people who are already customers.

column2: >Online advertising in Kenya in 5 simple steps
>Now that we have covered benefits, paid and organic and types of online advertising in Kenya you might be wondering how to go about it.
column3: >In this section, we guide you through online advertising in Kenya in 5 simple steps.

column2: >1. Online marketing strategy
>For your online advertising in Kenya to succeed you need a campaign concept backed by research.
column3: >Begin by stating the problem you are trying to solve, and then connect this to the audience you are trying to reach.
column4: >For instance, are people landing on your website but then leaving right away without taking the desired action?
column5: >You could begin by looking at user behavior on google analytics which is a free Google tool.
column6: >This tool will help you understand what your customers are doing when they get to your website and also what they interact with just before they leave. You
column7: > could then come up with a strategy to improve your user experience. The high bounce rate could indicate that the website isn’t user-friendly. You
column8: > could then launch a campaign driving traffic to your website or landing page after you have improved the layout and observe the traffic behavior on Google analytics to see if it had improved.

column2: >2. Online advertising budgeting
>The online marketing budget for your online ads in Kenya should be simple. Begin with what you can afford. No need to start with a $1000 budget if that isn’t where your business is financially.

column4: > ads are pretty affordable. However, depending on the campaign objective you might want to go with Google even though Google ads might cost you more.

column2: >3. Ad creatives / Production
>The third stage of online advertising in Kenya is the creation of the banners, blogs, videos, and copies that will make the online advertisement. This
column3: > can be as simple or as intricate as you want depending on the budget, campaign objective, and the time you have.
column4: >When you’re beginning online advertising keep things simple.

>The fifth step of online marketing in Kenya is optimizing and reporting.

column5: >Ad optimization could vary greatly from changing the location, the target audience, the budget, or even the ad creative.

column1: 634,"Social media users in Kenya 2022","

column2: >Social media has changed the way individuals, organizations, and communities create, consume and share content. Social networks have helped people communicate and break geographical barriers that restricted instant communication, allowing successful social media collaborations.
column3: >Over the years, Kenya’s population has been on the rise to a whopping 55.60 million people according to
column4: >Global Digital Insights
column5: >. In this respect, there has been a rise in social media users in Kenya and social media services as well.
column6: >This article will take you through the social media applications in Kenya and their users.
column7: >There are roughly 11.7 million social media users in Kenya as of January 2022.

column2: >Facebook Users in Kenya
>Facebook is an American online social network service that is part of the company Meta Platforms.
column4: >Statcounter Global Stats
column5: >, the majority of mobile users in Kenya use Facebook to connect, communicate and access information. As of March 2022, there were over 12 million Facebook users.
column6: >This shows that 42.9 percent of Facebook users in Kenya are women. While Facebook’s largest audience was male users making up 57.1 percent of its user base.
column7: >The company revised the audience figures which show that Facebook’s ad reach in Kenya was equivalent to 17.9 percent of the total population at the start of 2022. Additionally, the reach in Kenya is equivalent to 42.6 percent of the local internet user base, regardless of age.

column2: >Facebook Messenger Users in Kenya
>Facebook Messenger is a non-free instant messaging platform and application developed by Meta Platforms.
column4: >Statista
column5: >, Facebook Messenger has a penetration rate of 19.7 percent in Kenya. A total of over 11 million users utilize the messaging platform for connection and communication purposes.
column6: >The largest audience of Facebook Messenger users in Kenya are from the age of 25 to 34 years and make up 35.1 percent of the user base. This is followed by users aged from 18 to 24 years.
column7: >Meta’s advertising research shows that ads on Facebook Messenger reached 1.90 million users in Kenya. While the revised audience numbers suggest that Messenger’s ad reach in Kenya was equivalent to 3.4 percent of the total population.
column8: >As of the start of the year, 45.2 percent of Facebook Messenger’s ad audience in Kenya was female while 54.8 percent was male.

column2: >YouTube Users in Kenya
>Youtube is an American online video-sharing platform that allows users to enjoy content or music or upload videos for public or private consumption.
column3: >Over the years there has been a rise in content creators using social media to push their respective Youtube channels. In Kenya, there is a variety of content creators who dabble in lifestyle, make-up, and comedy content which garner a lot of attention. I
column4: >n Kenya, there are 9.29 million users of YouTube as of early 2022. This means that its ad reach was equivalent to 16.7 percent of Kenya’s population at the start of the year. In-depth, that means that these ads reach 39.9 percent of Kenya’s total internet user base regardless of age.
column6: >As of January 2022, 42.7 percent of YouTuber’s audience is female, while 53.7 percent is male.

column2: >Twitter Users in Kenya
>Twitter is an American microblogging and social networking service communications company.
column3: >In Kenya, Twitter is used as a means of communication, connection, and sometimes accessing information. Most times Kenyans use Twitter as a way to share discord or share memes and debates on topics. Such an example of this is the #KenyansonTwitter, KOT for short.
column4: >As of early 2022, Twitter’s advertising resources show that Twitter had 1.35 million users. This means that the ad reach in Kenya is equivalent to 2.4 percent of the total population at the time.
column5: >The ad reach in Kenya is comparable to 5.8 percent of the local internet user base regardless of age.

column2: >LinkedIn Users in Kenya

>LinkedIn is an American business and employment-oriented online service that operates via websites. The platform is used primarily for professional networking and career development, to allow job seekers to link with potential employers.
column3: >The figures published by LinkedIn advertising research indicate that the platform had 2.90 million members.
column4: >The ad reach on LinkedIn shows that the audience in Kenya was equivalent to 5.2 percent of the total population at the start of 2022. In context, the ad reach in Kenya is comparable to 12.4 percent of the local internet user base.
column5: >As of early 2022, the largest audience reached on LinkedIn is male at 62.2 percent, while women make up 37.8 percent.

column2: >Instagram Users in Kenya

>Instagram is an American social networking service that focuses on photo and video sharing. This application allows its users to upload media that can be edited with filters and organized by the use of hashtags and geographical tagging.
column3: >Numbers published by Meta’s advertising tool indicate that in early 2022, Kenya had 2.50 million Instagram users. This suggests that the ad reach in Kenya was comparable to 4.5 percent of the total population.
column4: >It is also important to note that the application’s ad reach was equivalent to 10.7 percent of the local internet user base as of the beginning of 2022. It was also revealed that 54 percent of Instagram’s ad audience in Kenya was male, while 46.0 percent was male.

column2: >Snapchat Users in Kenya

>Snapchat is an American social network that works with the principal features that include pictures and messages that are available for a short amount of time before they become inaccessible to their recipients. It works as an instant messaging app and service.
column3: >In Kenya, Snapchat is used as a means of communication and in some cases, accessibility of information through Snapchat’s video series.
column4: >Data published by Snapchat’s adverting indicated that the app had gained 1.75 million users at the beginning of the year. This means that the ad reach was close to 3.1 percent of the total population.
column5: >The ad reach Snapchat has is equivalent to 7.5 percent of the local internet user base, as of January 2022. In that context,  28.1 percent reflects the male audience while 70.0 percent reflects the female audience.

column2: >Why is this information important?

>The statistics are important because although some Kenyans use traditional media to discover brands, social media makes it easier for brands to be discovered because it links them directly to their audience, through various social media apps.
>Conclusion

>When it comes to social media users in Kenya, it can be noted that they use social media primarily to connect with family and friends. Moreso, other than accessing content, it is used in the accessing of information and is an easy way to directly reach potential consumers.

column18: >To help you narrow down your search and find the best company for your needs, we will go through six important factors to consider before hiring an event planner. Plus, a list of the top six-event management companies in Kenya. Let us dive right in.

column2: >Factors to consider before hiring corporate event management companies in Kenya

>Event planning and management companies are not that different. Most, if not all, of these companies, will not only do managing of the event but the planning as well. However, do not go into the selection process blindly.
column3: >Hiring an event planning company in Kenya does not have to be a daunting task, but make sure you spend time sourcing the best event planners and screen them carefully. Outlined below are some steps to consider before hiring an event planner.

column2: >    1. Determine the objective of your corporate event

>Most people think that hiring an external event planner begins by determining the event’s budget, but the truth is that it’s more important to begin by defining why you want to hold an event in the first place.
column3: >Before you reach out to an external or internal resource that will help you plan that event, you want to be in a position to share the important goals of the event. Answer your own relevant questions about who, what, where, when, why and how. There will be plenty of time to make adjustments.

column2: >    2. Determine your reason for hiring an event planner

>Once you’ve defined your objectives, a few clear ideas will begin to emerge about what theme and message you want to communicate at your event. But most importantly, what activities and services do you need the external resource to handle on your behalf?
column3: >Will they help with selecting the venue? Will they build menus and make those recommendations? Are they helping with creating important communication items, such as invitations and other event materials? Do they need to source entertainment and speakers? Will they be needed on-site at the event? Will they handle event registration, etc? These are important questions to have figured out before you hire.

column2: >    3. Estimate a budget

>Based on your event objectives, it’s possible to create a general sense of how much it will cost for various elements of your program. This will vary based on the type of event you are hosting, and what it includes.
column3: >Many people who organise an event for the first time often fall into the trap of wanting to plan a champagne event on a soft drink budget (no offence intended to related-themed events—we love those, too). And that’s why many people turn to their event planners for help.

column2: >  4. Source a qualified event planner

>Regardless of whether it’s a social event or a corporate meeting, generally speaking, the rules of hiring an event planner remain the same. You want to hire someone who has expertise in your type of event to ensure maximum success.
column3: >If you’re trying to find the best event planner for your affair, it’s best to research someone who is experienced and holds a strong reputation within the community of event planners. Word of mouth provides an opportunity for easy sales for a planner wanting to find new clients, but peer reputation is very effective.

column2: >    5. Meet your planners in person if possible
>It’s not always possible to meet someone in person, especially if your program is out of town. However, depending on the budget and importance of your event, this is a very important step.
column3: >And it’s a step that should be invested in prior to narrowing your selected planner. Keep in mind, that the most highly experienced planner may not always be the best hire. You will gain a sense of someone’s passion and professionalism when you build a rapport with someone and listen to their ideas. Hence, the importance of meeting in person.

column2: >     6. Check references on your event planner(s)

>It’s not good enough to go on your gut instinct, the advice of your friends, or even colleagues and coworkers. This is your event, and your name and your reputation will be associated with it. Of course, you will ask for the names of clients who have worked with the planner before. And you’re likely to get favorable contacts.
column3: >But do more digging. Ask the event planner to talk about where they’ve held events before, and check those sources. Read information about their business and find your own references to check.

How Adoption of Learning Management Systems in Kenya(LMS) Can Drive Organisations Forward in Kenya

column2: >We would all agree that in today’s competitive business landscape, an organisation's short and long-term success heavily depends on the continuous training of its workforce.
column3: >One of the most advanced and widely used training technologies is the
column4: >Learning Management System
column5: > (LMS), a software application used to administer, deliver, and monitor employee training and educational programs.
column6: >Every organisation would like an informed, better-skilled employee with a continuous appetite for growth, but how do you successfully achieve this as an employer?
column7: >Well, in this blog we shall widely look at how you can adopt a Learning Management Systems in Kenya that adjusts to your business needs while upskilling your workforce.

column2: >Key Features of A Good Learning Management System
>As organisations across Kenya continue to adopt and embrace the benefits of Learning Management Systems, it’s important to take a look at some of its key features.
>Software Integration

>For a seamless, all-in-one learning and training platform, a good Learning Management System should have integrated software such as video conferencing tools to easily launch training within the platform.
>Collaboration and Communication Tools

>For a fast, simple learning process, collaborative and communication tools such as discussion forums, chat and messaging platforms are essential parts and parcels of a good learning management system.
>System Security
>We know how important it is to have a platform that protects the organisation and its users’ sensitive information.
column3: >When choosing a learning management system go for a platform that adheres to strong access control and the overall system security.

column2: >Different Content Delivery Formats
>Having the choice of submitting, accessing or issuing a task in either video, audio, or text format sets apart a good learning platform from the rest.
column3: >Therefore, a good learning system should have different formats that one can use when accessing content at their convenience.

column2: >Compatibility With Mobile Devices
>Unlike a physical learning classroom, a learning management system can be accessed from the comfort of your mobile device.
column3: >This ensures you aren't missing important updates or notifications whenever you're away from your computer.

column2: >Benefits of Adopting Learning Management Systemsin Kenya to Kenyan Organisations
>Adopting LMS for Kenyan organizations can be a game changer, an opportunity to widen growth, equip employees with new skills and increase overall work efficiency.
column3: >It’s also important to understand different types and commonly used learning management systems in the market and how their functionalities can help drive your organization forward.
column4: >Here are some of the main benefits of LMS to businesses, a system that has been the driving force for many businesses in Kenya.

column2: >Cost-Effective Learning
>We can all agree that traditional learning systems can be costly to organizations when you budget on traveling, trainer fees, and learning materials.
column3: >The learning management system has enabled organizations to train their workforce at a relatively cheaper cost, making it a system every business would adopt.

column2: >Time-Saving
>Learning management systems enable trainees to learn at their own pace, meaning the organizations will be gaining on the skills learned while maintaining the same workflow.
column3: >Not only does this save the organization time, but it also saves the money they would have spent organizing training.

column2: >Easy Progress and Performance Tracking
>Organisations can easily track the performance of trainees, ensuring that set targets and goals are met.
column3: >Performance upgrade suggestions reports can also be provided in situations where trainees fell short of the required performance targets.

column2: >Flexible Learning Process
>Employees can learn anytime, anywhere at their own pace while accessing learning materials through the platform. This reduces downtime while increasing overall productivity.
>Increased Profits and Productions
>Studies
column3: > suggest that organizations that invest in training their workforce achieve an average of 24 percent higher profit margins than companies with lower yearly training investments.
column4: >MLS training equips employees with the necessary skills to work and improve the organization’s productivity.

column2: >Conclusion- Learning Management System, The Driving Force for Kenyan Businesses

>Embracing LMS technology can drive organizations forward by empowering employees to continuously learn and grow, ultimately leading to improved performance and sustained success in the country’s competitive business environment.
column3: >With its seamless integration of software, collaboration tools, and mobile compatibility, LMS  provides an efficient and effective platform for upskilling any Kenyan organization's workforce.
column4: >But before settling for any learning management system, it is advisable for organizations to thoroughly research the LMS they would want, its features, and most importantly, the right company to help in the adoption process.

column4: >, a leading LMS provider in Kenya.

Website Development Pricing in Kenya: Understanding the Cost Factors

column2: >In this blog, we explore the concept of website development pricing in Kenya to help you make a strategically sound decision.
>Do you often find yourself shopping for a product or researching a company online before considering a visit to their physical store?
>With approximately
column4: >of Kenyans shopping online since the onset of the Covid19, there's no doubt that a superb website is now a necessity to propel your business forward.

column2: >So, the question is no longer whether you need a website but rather, what's the cost of developing a website that aligns with your business needs?
>In this article, we'll take an in-depth look at the key determinants of website development pricing in Kenya, and how you can effectively budget for your website revamp or a whole new website.

column1: Factors Affecting Website Development Pricing in Kenya

column2: >A question we often receive from Kenyan businesses is why it’s difficult to fully determine the cost of developing a website
>To address this question, let's look at this analogy
>Imagine you're planning to build a house, and you have the same question: “What is the cost of building a house?”

>Just as the cost of a house can vary significantly based on factors such as the type of house, the number of rooms or floors, interior and exterior finishes, and various other considerations, the same principle applies to the development of a website.
>Below is a comprehensive look at the factors affecting the cost of web development in Kenya.

>Your website's domain name is the foundation of your online presence. It's crucial to understand that the cost of your domain name can vary depending on the type you choose. The most common choices are .com domains or top-level domains (TLDs).

>The choice between a .com and a TLD largely depends on your website's purpose and your brand identity. While .com domains are versatile and budget-friendly, TLDs offer a unique touch and can help your website stand out.
>What is your purpose for the website, is it an informational website, e-commerce or custom website?

>Given the intricate elements such as integrations, CMS, email marketing tools, shopping carts, and product catalogs, among others, the cost of developing e-commerce, for example, can be significantly higher compared to creating an informational website.
>Developing a website on WordPress can be a more budget-friendly option compared to creating one from scratch. However, cost is just one aspect to consider in this decision.
>While the cost of WordPress is an attractive feature, it's equally crucial to choose a platform that not only aligns with your budget but also meets your specific website requirements.
>Content Management Systems, commonly known as CMS, are prebuilt platforms that streamline the process of creating, editing, and managing website content.
>CMS platforms not only enhance efficiency but also empower individuals and organizations to take control of their online presence.

>While many CMS options are open source and free to use, it's essential to note that the choice of CMS design can influence the cost. For example, platforms like Wix may come with associated expenses.
Functionalities
>Integrating features like custom forms, social media connectivity, live chat, or advanced search functionality can lead to an increase in the overall price of website development.
>The complexity of your design directly correlates with the time and resources required for development.
>Consequently, the more intricate and feature-rich your website design, the greater the investment needed in terms of both time and budget.
Maintenance
>Website hosting is an essential service that ensures your website is both visible and accessible on the internet.
>The cost of hosting can vary significantly, depending on several factors, including the hosting provider you choose, the specific hosting plan you opt for, and the level of support you require.
>For instance, shared hosting may offer a more budget-friendly option, but it might be less convenient when compared to dedicated hosting.

>On the other hand, when we talk about website maintenance costs, we're referring to the expenses associated with tasks such as bug fixes, updates, security scans, and more. These costs can fluctuate based on the type and complexity of your website.
>
>Your website is the vital first point of contact between your business and its audience. It’s the online face of your company, shaping the initial impression your customers form.
>Whether you opt for a simple or complex website design, it's imperative to consider the cost of website development as a strategic, long-term investment in your business's success.
>When you're on the lookout for a website development partner in Kenya, it's important to choose a company that not only boasts experience but is also known for its solid reputation.

column2: >Have you ever scrolled through Facebook and seen those businesses crushing it with their social media game?
>“Kenya had 10.55 million social media users in January 2026” -
>With more and more joining each year the opportunities for businesses are huge.
>But how do you break through the crowd and grab your audience's attention? That's where creating a killer social media marketing campaign comes in.
>

>This blog post is your roadmap to social media success in Kenya, and I'll show you exactly how to craft a campaign that resonates with your audience, drives results, and puts your business on the map.
>So, get ready to unlock the true potential of social media. Let's dive in!

column1: Understanding Social Media Marketing and Why It Matters for Kenyan Business

column2: >
>Creating a successful social media marketing campaign isn't as complicated as it might seem. Not when you have a good idea of your target audience and business objectives.

>Social media platforms like Facebook, Instagram, and Twitter offer a direct line for businesses to connect with their target audience, and with a good social media marketing campaign you can take them through the phases from awareness right to conversion
>In a country like Kenya with increasing internet access, people are spending more and more time scrolling and chatting on these apps daily.
>That's why having a social strategy could work magic for your business trying to get its name out there!

column1: How to Create a Social Media Marketing Campaign in Kenya:

column2: >
>1. Define Your Goals: What Do You Want to Achieve?
>The first step is to define a goal for your campaign, whatever your ultimate aim, and make it clear, specific, and measurable.
>Setting goals like ""increased brand awareness"" is great, but how will you measure that?

>Aim for quantifiable targets like ""reaching 10,000 new followers in 3 months"" or ""boosting website traffic by 20%."" This focus will guide your content strategy and help you keep track of your progress.
>2.  Know Your Audience: Who Are You Talking To?
>To resonate with your audience, you must understand them inside and out.
>Forget generic demographics – delve deeper into their interests, aspirations, and online behavior. What kind of content do they engage with? What challenges do they face?
>Research through surveys, competitor analysis, and social listening tools to see what type of content your audience tends to incline to.
>These insights will help you craft content that speaks their language and addresses their needs, not just yours.
>3. Crafting Compelling Content: What to Share with Your Audience?
>Now comes the fun part:
column3: >Create content that stops the scroll and makes them stick around a bit more.

column2: >Audiences crave authenticity, humor, and cultural relevance. Think of high-quality visuals, catchy captions in the common language, and stories that resonate with their everyday lives.
>Remember, valuable content doesn't always mean promoting your product.
>Educate, entertain, and inspire your audience
column3: they'll become loyal brand advocates in due time.

column2: >4. Choosing the Right Platform: Where to Reach Your Audience?
>Not all social media platforms are good for your brand.
>Facebook might reign supreme for older audiences, Instagram might resonate better with the youth, and LinkedIn might be better for Business-to-Business products, etc.
>Consider your target demographic and campaign goals. E.g. If you're targeting young professionals,  LinkedIn and Twitter might be better platforms
>Don't spread yourself thin – master one or two platforms before venturing further. Remember, you can always expand later based on your success.
>5. Engaging with Your Audience: Building a Community
>Social media is a two-way street. Don't just broadcast, build relationships!
>Respond to comments promptly, answer questions with enthusiasm, and show your audience you care.
>Your community is your biggest asset. Treat them with respect, value their feedback, and watch your brand loyalty soar.
>6. Measuring Success: Tracking Your Results
>Your data is your compass on the social media journey. Set key performance indicators (KPIs) aligned with your goals.
>Monitor reach and engagement metrics. Analyze your performance regularly and don't be afraid to adapt. Data-driven decisions will keep your campaign on track and help you maximize your impact.

column1: Common Types of Influencer Marketing in Kenya

column2: >Most, if not all successful influencer marketing campaigns follow the below guidelines when selecting the ideal influencer.

column1: Analyze the Niche and Reach of Potential Influencers

column2: >Analyzing potential influencers is crucial when evaluating whether their niche and reach align with your brand.
>A thorough assessment of an influencer includes assessing whether their niche and reach complement the core offerings of your brand.

>For instance, if a tour campaign focuses on unique off-the-beaten-path adventures or luxurious travel experiences, it is crucial to partner with a travel influencer whose content aligns with the brand's essence.
>These factors allow businesses to collaborate with influencers who resonate with their goals, ensuring an impactful campaign.

column1: Have an Outline of Your Campaign Goals

column2: >Before collaborating with an influencer, it is crucial to establish clear campaign goals or metrics. Ensure that these objectives are documented and tracked consistently, either at the campaign's conclusion or throughout its progress.
>Monitoring your influencer marketing campaigns in alignment with your objectives enables you to make essential tweaks and enhance the campaign for improved results.
>One common mistake made by many businesses is hastily choosing an influencer solely based on their large following.
>A not highly advisable way of selection.
>For example, you can pick an influencer with a handful of loyal and engaging followers rather than indifferent followers with high numbers, who are likely not to convert.
>For the content to connect with the intended influencer audience, high engagement and a substantial following are essential.
>This ensures that the campaign aligns with the interests and preferences of the audience the brand is targeting.

column1: Choose an Influencer with Whom You Share Values

column2: >Opt for an influencer whose values and principles align with yours. This choice ensures that the influencer not only promotes your brand but also shares a mutual understanding of core values.
>For example, if your brand is gender-conscious, you wouldn't want to collaborate with an influencer who holds different views and beliefs on the same.

column1: 2048,"The Role of Human-Centred Design in Creating Inclusive & Accessible Digital Products","<span style=""font-weight: 400
column2: >How inclusive and accessible are your digital products? Do they cater to the specific needs, pain points and preferences of your target audience?
>These questions lie at the heart of a crucial yet often overlooked aspect of business
column3: the design of digital products with a focus on the user.

column2: >Increasingly, businesses are turning to human-centred design, recognizing its vital role in creating digital products that truly meet the needs of users.
>It's the key factor that not only attracts users to your site but also retains their engagement and loyalty.
>Continue reading to discover how you can enhance user satisfaction through a human-centred design approach.
>Human-centred design
column3: > is a problem-solving technique that puts real people at the centre of the development process.

column2: >The goal is to keep users’ wants, pain points, and preferences front of mind during every phase of the process.
>By doing so, you can build more intuitive, accessible products that are more likely to be adopted by users.

column1: The Process of Creating a Human-Centered Design

column2: >We’ll guide you through some of the key stages of the human-centred design process, further exploring each step in detail and providing practical tips for creating user-centric designs.
> Empathy works well when you want to have a deep understanding of the users' needs, desires and possible challenges.
>To develop empathy for the target audience, methods such as user interviews, observations, and
column4: > may be used to gather insights.

column2: >: To uncover underlying needs, brands should directly engage with users, listen actively, and ask open-ended questions.
>In this stage, insights gathered during the empathise stage are synthesised to identify user needs and define design opportunities.
>So, how are the insights synthesised?
>The insights are filtered into clear design objectives and defining success criteria for the project.
>: Use tools such as user personas, journey maps, and problem statements to articulate user needs and design goals effectively.
>Ideation is a creative process where designers gather with open minds to generate a wide range of possible solutions to address the defined design challenges.
>Techniques such as brainstorming, sketching, and mind mapping are used to gather ideas in a facilitated, judgement-free environment.
>: Encourage divergent thinking, suspend judgment, and prioritize quantity over quality during ideation sessions to foster creativity.
>Prototyping involves creating tangible representations from paper to digital, the aim is to capture and test design concepts.
>Prototypes can range from low-fidelity sketches and wireframes to high-fidelity mockups and interactive prototypes.
>: Start with low-fidelity prototypes to gather feedback early and iterate rapidly. Gradually increase fidelity as the design evolves.
>The testing stage involves identifying techniques, scenarios, data, cases and the expected results.
>User testing sessions, usability studies, and A/B testing are used to identify usability issues and validate design decisions.
>While understating how to conduct a design test is vital, identifying the
column4: > is equally important.

column2: >: Involve users throughout the testing process, observe their behaviour, and listen to their feedback without bias. Iterate based on findings to refine the design further.
>Change is inevitable, and so are customers' behaviours and expectations which are evolving rapidly.
>Remaining competitive in the market requires taking action that prioritises your customers' needs and adapts to meet their expectations.
>Here are some of the benefits of designing human-centred products and services.

>Human-centred design prioritises the needs of users. Therefore, a brand that designs products or services that align with user preferences, behaviours, and goals will ultimately record high user satisfaction levels.
>When users feel that a product or service has been designed to address their specific needs and challenges, they are more likely to express satisfaction.
>The ease of accessing or using a product or service is a core focus of human-centred design.
>Brands can improve usability through user research, testing, and interactive design processes.
>In the long run, it enhances user experience, reduces frustration and creates a more successful interaction with the product or service.
>The costs of rework and product failure can be staggering and unmanageable for businesses.
>However, by involving users early and often in the design process, brands can identify potential issues and opportunities for improvement before significant resources are invested.
>Additionally, businesses can reduce the likelihood of costly post-launch modifications or fixes by creating products that meet user needs.
>Services or products that are designed with the user in mind are likely to be adopted and used consistently.
>By understanding user motivations and behaviours, human-centred design helps identify opportunities to enhance the product or service in ways that encourage continued usage and loyalty.
>There’s a significant competitive advantage in the marketplace when products or services are created with the user in mind.
>Brands can further stay ahead in the industry by continuously bettering their digital products based on user feedback and market insights.

column1: 2273,"Custom Vs Off-The-Shelf Software: What’s The Right Choice for Kenyan Businesses?","<!-- wp:paragraph -->

Choosing the right software can be daunting, especially in Kenya's dynamic and ever-evolving tech landscape.

This blog is your guide through this critical decision. We'll delve into the key differences between custom and off-the-shelf software, explore the unique advantages custom solutions offer Kenyan businesses, and help you navigate the potential drawbacks to make an informed choice.
Difference between Custom vs. Off-the-Shelf Software Solutions

Custom and off-the-shelf software solutions differ in several important ways that impact their viability for businesses. Evaluating these distinctions enables organizations to match their needs and capabilities most effectively. One crucial factor to consider is the cost of custom software development in Kenya, which may have higher initial costs but can potentially offer lower long-term expenses.
Let’s see which one will suit your business best.
Difference between custom and off-the-shelf software solutions:

Your choice depends on your business needs, budget, and future growth plans. Custom software offers a perfect fit, but if you're on a tight budget or your needs are common, off-the-shelf software might be a good starting point.
‘A hybrid approach – using off-the-shelf software as a base with custom add-ons – can also be a clever solution.’
Why is Custom Software Important for Kenyan businesses?

While off-the-shelf software might seem like a tempting shortcut, navigating Kenya's dynamic business landscape with custom software can help you tackle the unique terrain and challenges Kenyan businesses face. Building custom software in Kenya is essential to address specific industry needs, from managing mobile money transactions to optimizing logistics for rural areas.
According to a study - “62% of businesses prefer custom software development over off-the-shelf solutions due to the need for tailored functionality and scalability.” Source- lvivity.com
Let's face it, Kenya's business environment presents distinct hurdles that show us the importance of custom software solutions in Kenya.

column1: 2352,"Five Legal Requirements for Events Planning in Cameroon","<!-- wp:paragraph --><!-- /wp:paragraph -->
Did you know your event could be cancelled if you overlook key legal requirements?
It happens more often than you'd think.
Many times, organisers fail to consider important legal criteria, which results in the event being cancelled or postponed.
These mistakes may result in costly setbacks, lost time, and, most importantly, harm to the reputation of your company.
From permits to licences and regulations, getting your event legally sound is one of the most crucial, but often overlooked, parts of event planning.
These legal aspects can be the difference between a smooth, enjoyable day and a stressful one riddled with unexpected complications.
Events Legal Requirements for Businesses in Cameroon
No one wants to see their party get crashed by legal troubles.
Planning an event is exciting, and it’s easy to get caught up in the fun stuff- venue decoration, music playlists, guest lists etc.
But ignoring the legal side of things can lead to big problems, such as fines, cancellation, or worse- a tarnished reputation.
Understanding these five essential event legal requirements in Cameroon will keep you in the clear and help you focus on making your event a success.
This is where you need to start.
Venue licensing for events is basically the “okay” from local authorities to hold an event at your chosen location. Without it, your event could be shut down before it even kicks off.
Fortunately, many venues already have a premises license in place. But don’t assume, double-check.
If the venue doesn’t have this license, it’s your responsibility to apply for one.
The application process may take time, so get this sorted early on.
Safety is the heart of a great event.
It’s not just about having fun, it’s also about ensuring everyone is safe while doing so.
Therefore, ensure you have emergency plans, crowd control measures, and even clean restroom facilities.
A lot of people tend to overlook things like fire exits or the accessibility of medical services on-site, but these are crucial in the overall event experience.
We all love a deliciously cooked meal, don’t we?
But if food safety isn’t on point, it can also turn an event into a disaster.
Whether you're bringing in outside caterers or handling food in-house, strict food hygiene practices need to be followed.
Ensure the people handling food are certified and trained in food safety practices.

In some cases, your local authorities might want to inspect your setup before you start serving. It’s a little extra effort that goes a long way toward ensuring your guests enjoy delicious, safe meals.
Events often come with lots of excitement, and with that excitement comes… noise.
Whether it’s music, announcements, or the general hum of people having fun, things can get loud.

But don’t forget that there are strict noise regulations in Cameroon, especially for events that run late into the night. Each location has its own noise limits, so be sure to understand these ahead of time.
This is one area that often slips through the cracks,
But it’s essential to ensure your event is accessible to everyone, including people with disabilities.
Ensuring wheelchair access, appropriate seating, accessible bathrooms and easy-to-navigate pathways create an inclusive and welcoming environment.
Plus, in some cases, not providing proper access is against the law, so it’s something you can’t afford to miss.
Conclusion: Event Legal Requirements in Cameroon-A Recipe for Success
Closely paying attention to the above simple yet crucial event legal requirements in Cameroon, sets you up for success.
But, keep in mind, that these aren’t just legal hoops to jump through, each requirement contributes to a smooth, enjoyable, and successful event.
And if you’re feeling a little overwhelmed, why not bring in the pros?

Their expertise ensures every event legal requirements in Cameroon are handled, leaving you to focus on what matters most, the agenda of the day.

3032,"Why We Are Rebranding","Over the years, Growthpad Consulting has partnered with various organizations seeking to achieve their objectives in the digital media and tech realm. Today, we embark on a significant new chapter in our journey. This rebranding is not merely about a new logo or fresh colors on our website
column2: it represents a profound transformation aimed at aligning with our future ambitions and reflecting the growth and evolution of our firm.

column1: This decision has been carefully considered. In recent years, we have experienced substantial growth, expanded our service offerings, and increased our impact across Africa and beyond.
Growthpad Consulting has evolved from a digital consulting firm into a professional services company with expertise in communication, market intelligence, innovation, and digital media.

As our firm has expanded, our brand must reflect the new breadth and depth of what we offer to clients. Rebranding allows us to clarify our identity and ensures it aligns with who we are today—not who we were when we started.
Rebranding allows us to clarify our identity and ensures it aligns with who we are today—not who we were when we started.

Our expanded scope responds to the evolving landscape of technology in the African digital space. According to reports by Digital Reality, Africa’s digital economy is expected to reach $180 billion by 2025 and a further $712 billion by 2050. At Growthpad, we are actively helping organizations tap into this opportunity.

Our core business now includes strategic communication, digital media solutions, and innovation consulting, each of which has grown by double digits over the past two years. For example, our communication services have expanded to encompass comprehensive media strategies, stakeholder engagement, and crisis communication. We have supported organizations in navigating complex socio-political landscapes in diverse countries across Africa and globally. Our expertise in crafting narratives that resonate with unique audiences has positioned us as a trusted partner for both local and international businesses.

This expanded scope necessitates a fresh identity—one that mirrors the sophistication and diversity of the services we offer. Our previous brand, Growthpad Digital Consulting, no longer encapsulates the multifaceted nature of our work. By rebranding to Growthpad Consulting Group, we are removing the ""Digital"" label, signaling that while digital remains at our core, we are much more than digital consultants. We are communication experts, innovation strategists, and digital media specialists working at the forefront of Africa’s transformation.

A critical factor behind our rebranding is our Pan-African ambition. Africa is a continent on the rise, rich with opportunities, and we see ourselves as key players in driving its progress. According to the African Development Bank, Africa’s infrastructure investment needs amount to between $130 and $170 billion per year, with a financing gap of $68 to $108 billion annually. Additionally, the World Economic Forum estimates that Africa’s population will reach 2.5 billion by 2050, with 60% under the age of 25. This demographic dividend, coupled with the rise of a digital economy, provides fertile ground for businesses and governments to innovate and grow.

However, navigating Africa’s complex business environments presents unique challenges. Each African country operates within its distinct socio-political and economic context. Our clients need more than a consulting firm—they need a partner who understands these complexities and can help them thrive in Africa’s fast-changing landscape.

Growthpad Consulting is positioning itself to be that partner. Our rebranding symbolizes our deep commitment to being a Pan-African leader in communication and digital innovation. The new identity incorporates African symbols and motifs, representing our deep roots on the continent while projecting confidence, trust, and professionalism to our global partners.
[caption id="""" align=""alignnone"" width=""640""] Growthpad Consulting Group Rebrand In Africa[/caption]
A Competitive Edge Through Innovation and Trust

Another driving force behind our rebranding is the need to differentiate ourselves in an increasingly competitive market. According to the World Bank, foreign direct investment in Africa reached $83 billion in 2021, an increase of 37% from the previous year. As more global organizations invest in Africa, the demand for professional services firms that can deliver innovative solutions has never been higher.

What sets Growthpad apart is our commitment to innovation, our deep understanding of digital trends, and our focus on building long-term relationships based on trust. Over the last seven years, we’ve built a solid reputation, working with clients across multiple sectors, including telecommunications, the development sector, financial services, healthcare, and the public sector. Notable organizations we’ve partnered with include USAID in Kenya, Ecobank in West Africa, the International Fund for Animal Welfare (IFAW) across Africa, Uber in East Africa, and UKAID in East Africa.

We understand that maintaining our competitive edge requires continuous evolution, and this rebranding reflects our future-forward approach. Our new identity embodies our position at the cutting edge of communication, innovation, and digital transformation.

In addition to our expertise in communication, innovation, and digital media, Growthpad Consulting Group has built a new suite of capabilities and a strong network of partnerships that enhance our ability to deliver comprehensive solutions. Our strategic brands—such as GCG Communication, GCG Events, Pine Market Intelligence, Video Force, GCG Dev, WeComply Labs, GCG Digital Agency, and Sqillsuite—allow us to extend our reach and capabilities across various sectors. These specialized arms bring deep market insights, innovative solutions, and world-class services to help our clients succeed in Africa's dynamic business landscape.

We leverage the unique strengths of our partners to ensure that every project benefits from best-in-class expertise, whether in market research, video production, event management, or regulatory compliance. These collaborations enable us to offer seamless, end-to-end solutions that empower organizations to thrive and grow sustainably.

Our new brand identity includes colors and design elements that evoke professionalism, reliability, and authenticity, paired with our commitment to delivering exceptional results. We want our brand to visually represent our dedication to being a trusted advisor and strategic partner for organizations navigating Africa’s dynamic markets.
Rooted in Tradition, Looking to the Future

Our rebranding is not just about where we are today but also about where we are headed. As we look to the future, we aim to ensure that our brand remains modern and relevant while staying rooted in our African heritage. Africa is a continent of rich traditions, diverse cultures, and untapped potential. Our new logo, color palette, and design motifs incorporate subtle African elements that tell the story of our origins and honor the traditions that have shaped who we are.
At the same time, we are forward-thinking. As Africa rises, Growthpad Consulting rises with it. We are ready to embrace the challenges and opportunities that come our way.
This rebranding is more than a visual makeover
column2: it aligns us with the future, reflects our expanded scope of services, and positions Growthpad Consulting as a Pan-African voice in communication, innovation, technology services, and digital media. We are committed to being the trusted partner for organizations looking to thrive in Africa, and our new identity will help us achieve that goal.

column1: 3440,"How to Establish a Strong Corporate Identity in Zambia","A strong corporate identity is essential to a successful brand in today's fast-paced business environment.
As competition intensifies by the day, your corporate identity will distinguish you from the rest, clearly communicate your values, and establish rapport with your audience.
Creating a corporate identity that’s internationally unique and appeals locally can be a game-changer in Zambia's dynamic and diverse market.
Whether you are an established business attempting to rebrand or a startup, the right strategies can make all the difference.
But how do you develop a corporate identity that connects with your target audience and drives business growth?
In this article, we talk about how to build a strong corporate identity in Zambia and how it affects business growth.
In simple terms, it is how your business presents itself to the outside world.
The term ""corporate identity"" describes a group of visual and non-visual components that specify how your company is portrayed to the outside world.
These elements give your business distinctive recognition. They form an integral part of the process of corporate identity development in Zambia.
• Visual Elements: Your logo, colour scheme, typography, and other design elements.
• Core Values: The principles that guide your business decisions.
• Brand Messaging: The tone and language you use to communicate with your audience.
• Customer Experience: How your customers perceive your brand through interactions and services.

The designing of digital media for corporate identity should be a meticulous and intentional process aligning with the company's mission and vision. When done right, corporate identity ensures your business is recognisable, relatable, and unique. Your identity should address the main questions, like:
• Who are you as a business?
• What value do you offer to customers?
• Why should people trust you over competition?
Why Does Corporate Identity Matter for Zambian Businesses?
In Zambia, where the economy is driven by sectors like mining, tourism, and agriculture, corporate identity is essential to the success of businesses.
Benefits of corporate identity for business growth:
• Fosters Trust in the Brand: Building brand trust through corporate identity ensures customers engage with the business openly and repeatedly.
• Enhances Brand Recall: A unique corporate identity ensures your business stands out.

column2: Investors: A strong corporate image represents professionalism and stability.

column1: • Drives Growth: Effective brand strategies can capture market share and expand.

The answer to the question, ""Why does my business need a corporate identity?"" is therefore straightforward: It serves as the cornerstone for fostering enduring success and customer loyalty. How corporate identity impacts customer perception directly affects how your brand is promoted by loyal customers.
“Your brand is what other people say about you when you’re not in the room.” – Jeff Bezos, CEO of Amazon
Steps to Create a Unique Corporate Identity in Zambia
1. Define the DNA of Your Brand

An effective corporate identity depends on understanding your brand’s purpose and values. It's crucial to take into account not only what your company does but also why it does it and how it engages with its target market.

column2: text=Sometimes%20Brand%20DNA%20is%20only,expressed%20as%20a%20positioning%20phrase.""> brand's DNA entails determining:

column1: • The core principles that guide your business decisions.
• The unique value proposition to your customers.
• How you want your brand to be perceived by your audience.
In your corporate branding strategies, pay attention to the principles that align with your audience's values and industry standards.

Your brand’s digital media is often the first interaction people have with your brand, therefore serving as a critical component of corporate identity. Along with drawing attention, powerful images convey the character and principles of your company.
• Use colours and designs that reflect your brand’s personality.
• Include components that help your audience relate to you on an emotional level.
• Ensure consistency across platforms, from your website to packaging and advertising.
Visuals are non-negotiable—they’re the most immediate way your audience recognises and connects with your brand.

Visual identity as a part of corporate branding cannot work without impactful communication. How you communicate is just as important as what you communicate. Clarity, consistency, and alignment with your values are essential components of your brand messaging. It should have a tone that appeals to your audience and upholds the identity of your brand.
• Use a tone that is professional yet approachable.
• Highlight key values, such as reliability, quality, and social impact, that matter to your audience.
• Share stories that demonstrate your brand’s commitment to solving problems or making a difference.
Your messaging should consistently convey your brand's essential identity and values, whether it be through press releases or social media posts.

In the current digital era, your company's identity is greatly influenced by your online presence. Your brand will be recognisable, approachable, and interesting on all online platforms if you have a solid digital strategy.
• Create a user-friendly, responsive website that captures the core values of your brand
• Optimize your content for search engines to improve visibility and establish a connection with your target audience
• Make strategic use of social media channels to interact with clients directly and foster brand loyalty.
Your online presence should seamlessly integrate with your overall corporate identity, offering a consistent and compelling experience for users.
Developing a meaningful corporate identity requires active community engagement. It enhances your standing as a reliable brand and shows your company's dedication to having a positive influence.
How you can foster community connections:
• Support local initiatives, events, or programs that align with your brand values.
• Collaborate with nonprofits or other organisations to address social or environmental challenges.
• Share stories of your community engagement efforts to showcase your impact.
In addition to building goodwill, these actions humanise your brand, increasing its relatability and memorability.

Your corporate identity is only as strong as the experiences your customers have with your brand. Building credibility and trust requires consistently delivering high-quality work and keeping your word.
• Delivering dependable, superior goods and services that satisfy clients.
• Taking proactive steps to gather feedback and apply it to enhance your services.
• Bringing all facets of your company's operations into line with the principles you advocate.
By being dependable and consistent, you will establish respect and trust between your brand and clients.

The process of creating a corporate identity is continuous and integrates customer experiences, visuals, and values to create a unified brand. Every action you take, from clarifying the goal of your brand, refining your messaging, or interacting with the community improves your brand reputation and influence.

A strong corporate identity is not only advantageous in Zambia's fast-paced business landscape but essential. It's what gives your brand credibility and recall value and makes it ready to thrive in a dynamic market.
Get started right away and set up your company for success with a corporate identity that reflects your brand.

3451,"10 Comprehensive Guide to Choosing the Best Communication Agency in Cameroon","
Isn't it funny how every agency claims they're the best? Well, we’re not saying they're wrong…
But how do you separate an agency that walks the talk from the smooth talkers?
Whether you're launching a brand, managing a PR crisis, or simply trying to stay ahead in the competition, choosing the best communication agency in Cameroon can make all the difference.
This guide breaks down everything you need to know to make a smart, confident choice.
Before you even begin your search for the best communication agency in Cameroon, it’s important to assess your needs.
Having a clear understanding of your objectives will help guide your decision and streamline communication with prospective agencies.

column2: Review

column1: An agency can have the flashiest website and the smoothest pitch, but their real value is in their work. Check out their previous campaigns and what people say about them.
Who have they worked with? What are they saying? Did they help those brands shine?

column2: check their clients’ social media pages, PR mentions, and engagement levels. If their work speaks volumes, you’re onto something. If not, keep looking.

column1: Size matters, at least when choosing the best communication agency in Cameroon.
Big agencies look impressive. They have teams, offices, and fancy case studies. Small agencies, on the other hand, often bring agility, creativity, and personalized service.

It depends on your needs. If you’re a multinational company expanding into Cameroon, a bigger agency with a global network might be the way to go. But if you’re a startup looking for out-of-the-box strategies, a smaller, more flexible agency might serve you better.
Cameroon is a unique mix of cultures, languages, and business landscapes. An agency that understands the local scene will always have the upper hand.

They’ll know that what works in one part of the country won’t necessarily work in another. They’ll understand the unspoken rules of communication in different communities. And they’ll have the right media connections to make things happen.
Therefore, don't just settle for a local agency but one experienced running similar campaigns in the country.
You wouldn’t hire someone just based on their CV, right?
The same applies to choosing the best communication agency in Cameroon.
It's important to meet the team that will be handling your brand.
Are they excited about your brand? Do they ask the right questions? Do they listen, or are they just pitching?
Your agency is an extension of your team, so if the chemistry is off, it’s a red flag.
Hidden costs, vague deliverables, ghosting clients when things go south. No, thank you.
A good agency is clear about pricing, timelines, and what’s included in their services. They should also be open about what they can’t do.
If an agency promises the moon without explaining how - don’t commit.
“We’ll increase your engagement.” Nice. But by how much? “We’ll boost your brand awareness.” Cool. But where’s the strategy?
A solid agency doesn’t just throw around fancy marketing jargon. They have measurable goals and a roadmap to get there.
Ask for case studies, data, or testimonials. If their past work shows real, tangible impact, you’re on the right track.
Contracts aren’t just paperwork, they set the tone for your partnership. Before you sign, read every detail. Check for things like:
• Payment terms- Check for any hidden fees
• Termination clauses- Get to fully know what happens if you termite the contract.
• Ownership of content- Agree on who owns the work after the contract ends.
If anything feels off, ask. A great agency will thoroughly explain every bit of the contract.
But settling for an agency just because they’re cheap is a gamble with your brand.
A slightly pricier agency that delivers results is better than a bargain deal that wastes your time and money and potentially, your brand reputation.

Because when you find the right agency, everything clicks

3456,"Steps For Developing an Effective Communication Strategy for Businesses in Togo","A communication strategy is a critical part of any business
column2: it’s what shapes how your brand is seen and heard.

column1: A well-developed strategy aligns your team, refines your messaging, and ensures your audience hears exactly what they need to.
Without one, misunderstandings creep in, goals get lost in translation, and your brand voice weakens.
So, how do you build a strategy that keeps everything on track?
Buckle up, let’s break it down.
A communication strategy is a structured plan that outlines how your business will connect with customers, investors, and stakeholders, basically, everyone who matters to your success.
Thorough research, deliberate panning and perfect execution can tighten up your company’s current comms strategy or help you develop a brand-new one.
Here are five essential tips on how to develop a communication plan:
Your message needs to fit your audience, or you’re just shouting into the void.
• What keeps them up at night besides Netflix?
• Where do they hang out - social media, events, WhatsApp groups?
• How do they prefer to receive information - videos, texts, emails?

column1: 3727,"Guide to Grant winning proposals for African NGOs in 2026","<span style=""font-weight: 400
column2: >Grants remain a key source of funding for African NGOs. They help scale programs and expand impact. But competition is growing. Donors now expect clarity, accountability, and measurable outcomes.
>If you’re submitting proposals in 2025, it’s not enough to have a good idea. You need to show funders that your organization is credible, your project is feasible, and your outcomes are measurable.
>Here’s a step-by-step guide on writing grant proposals that meet those expectations.
>Before you start drafting, learn what the donor focus is. Read their funding guidelines, visit their website, and review their annual reports. Look at projects they’ve funded in the past.

>If they focus on youth employment, and you’re running a job training program, explain how your work aligns with their priorities. Use their language. If they mention “inclusive economic growth,” use that term (if it makes sense for your project).
>The clearer you are about this, the easier it is for the donor to see why your proposal fits.

column1: 2. Back Up Your Problem Statement With Data

column2: >Start your proposal with a clear problem statement. What issue are you addressing? Who is affected? Why is it urgent?

>Use data. If you have a needs assessment or baseline study, reference it. If you’ve done surveys or gathered feedback from the community, include those insights. Donors want evidence that you understand the issue on the ground—not assumptions.
>For example:

>“In Kwale County, 35% of households rely on unsafe water sources. This has led to high rates of waterborne diseases. Children under five are the most affected. Diarrhea accounts for 20% of deaths in this age group (Source: 2023 Ministry of Health Report).”
>Specific numbers give your proposal weight.

column1: 3. Present a Solid Theory of Change

column2: >A Theory of Change shows how your project will create impact. Start with the problem, explain your intervention, and describe the results you expect.
>Example:
>“If rural health clinics receive solar-powered refrigeration units, they can store vaccines safely. This will increase immunization rates and reduce preventable diseases in remote areas.”
>Keep it simple. Donors aren’t looking for buzzwords. They want to know that your approach makes sense.
>Funders don’t just fund projects—they fund impact. A strong proposal clearly demonstrates measurable outcomes, accountability, and alignment with donor priorities.
>Your objectives should be Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, and Time-bound.
>Not this:
>“Improve economic opportunities for young people.”
>This:
>“Install 100 hand-pump wells in rural communities in Northern Ghana by June 2025.”
>This level of clarity shows that you’ve thought through what you want to achieve—and how you’ll measure success.
>Most donors want to see a Logical Framework. It organizes your project into clear sections: objectives, activities, outputs, outcomes, indicators, and means of verification.
> isn’t just a table to fill out. It shows that your project is well planned and that you’ve thought through how activities lead to outcomes.
>Here’s an example:
aria-level=""1""><span style=""font-weight: 400
column3: >Objective: Improve primary school attendance in rural Malawi.

column2: aria-level=""1""><span style=""font-weight: 400
column3: >Output: Distribute school uniforms and provide daily meals to 1,000 students.

column2: aria-level=""1""><span style=""font-weight: 400
column3: >Outcome: Increase school attendance by 50% over two academic terms.

column2: aria-level=""1""><span style=""font-weight: 400
column3: >Means of Verification: School attendance records and community surveys.

column2: >Your Logframe should be simple and logical. Donors want to see how each part of your project connects and how you’ll measure success.

column2: E Plan)
>Donors expect a Monitoring and Evaluation (M&amp
column3: E) Plan. It should explain how you’ll collect data, what indicators you’ll track, and how often you’ll report results.

column2: >Start with baseline data and set clear targets. For example, you could track the percentage of trainees employed at three and six months after graduation.
>Good monitoring builds trust. It shows you’re serious about learning and improving—not just ticking boxes.

column1: 7. Prepare a Clear and Honest Budget

column2: >Your budget should match your activities. If you’re running training programs, the costs should include trainers’ fees, training materials, venue hire, and meals. Don’t inflate numbers. Don’t guess.
>Include a budget narrative that explains each line item. For example:
>“Trainer fees: $200 per day for 20 days, totaling $4,000.”
>Donors also like to see cost-effectiveness. If you can show that your program delivers good value (e.g., cost per beneficiary), include that.
>If you have co-funding or in-kind contributions, mention them. It shows you’re not relying entirely on one donor.
>Donors will ask how your project continues after their funding ends. Your Sustainability Plan should answer this.
>Can local partners take over? Are you building capacity so communities can manage programs themselves? Is there a path to generating income that supports future costs?
>Be practical. If you’re not sure, say how you plan to explore options during the project.
>No project is risk-free. Donors want to know that you’ve thought about what could go wrong—and how you’ll respond.
>Include a simple Risk Management Plan. Identify potential risks (e.g., low participant turnout, political instability) and explain how you’ll manage them.
>For example:
>“If recruitment is slow, we will work with local leaders to increase community awareness and trust.”
>Donors invest in organizations they can trust. Use your Organizational Background section to show your experience.

>Mention similar projects you’ve completed. Include any independent evaluations or impact reports you’ve done. If you have strong governance (e.g., board oversight, financial audits), include that too.
>If you’re new to grant funding, highlight your partnerships or the experience of your team members.
>Good grant proposals are clear, direct, and honest. They show that you understand the problem, have a practical solution, and can deliver results.

column2: >In today's market, customer loyalty is fragile.
>A single bad experience is all it takes for someone to walk away and find a competitor with a better offer.

column2: >But how do you know if you're actually succeeding?

column4: > metrics. These powerful tools replace guesswork with real, actionable data, revealing how your customers truly feel about your product, service, or support.

column2: >So, which metrics are the most important for driving real impact in 2026? Let's look into the key ones you should be paying attention to.
>Customer satisfaction metrics are measurements that help you understand how satisfied or unsatisfied your customers are with your products, services, and support.
>Instead of working on assumptions, these
column4: >give you clear insights you can use.

column2: >Tracking customer satisfaction goes beyond fixing problems. It’s about building loyalty, reducing churn, and strengthening retention. The right customer experience KPIs act like a real-time health check for your business.

column1: Importance of Customer Satisfaction Metrics for Businesses

column2: >Sales alone don’t tell the full story.
>A customer who buys once and never returns doesn’t drive long-term growth. Measuring customer satisfaction fills in that gap.
>Here’s why these metrics matter:

column2: >Think of customer satisfaction metrics as your early warning system

column1: Top 7 Customer Satisfaction Metrics to Track in 2026
1. Customer Satisfaction Score (CSAT)

column2: >The CSAT score is one of the simplest and most common ways to measure customer happiness. After an interaction (like a support call or product delivery), customers rate their satisfaction on a scale, often 1–5.
>It gives you instant feedback on specific interactions and shows where service quality needs improvement.
>NPS measures how likely customers are to recommend your brand to others, usually on a scale of 0–10.
>NPS is a powerful
column4: > metric, showing whether your customers are promoters who spread good word-of-mouth or detractors who may churn.

column2: >CES looks at how easy or difficult it is for customers to solve their issues with your company.
>It's important because customers don’t want to waste time. A low effort score signals efficiency in support, while a high one signals frustration.
>So, what is customer churn rate?
>This measures the percentage of customers who stop doing business with you over a set period.
>High churn points to poor satisfaction or weak loyalty. It’s one of the clearest customer experience KPIs for long-term growth.
>Retention shows the percentage of customers who stay with you over time.
>Strong customer retention metrics mean you’re meeting expectations and building loyalty, and it’s almost always cheaper than acquiring new ones.
>FCR measures whether customer issues are resolved on the first interaction.
>Customers hate being passed around or waiting days for solutions. High FCR builds trust and loyalty.
>This tracks how long it takes your team to resolve customer issues.
>The faster you solve problems, the higher the satisfaction levels. Delays usually result in poor reviews and potential churn.
